- Found: after the load bar hit 100 %, createWalk still ran its whole LATE section (roster foxes, cluster lobbies, robot factory, fire / news / TV / radio / tabloid, Vax / Salt / Pepper / Machine HQs, woodshop, dump, outlet crew, hardware, royal pad, Rob, 3 farms, outlets, gallery, offices, relics, 4 apartment towers, town life, cave, raft, pearl dive, sweep) + the skate course, ≈ 60 s in my preview, and GO TO MERU waited for all of it. Its dynamic imports were also fetched one after another (clusters alone 14.5 s, mostly network).
- Now (worlds/meru2-walk.js): (1) every module the build imports later is fetched in parallel at the start of createWalk; (2) the late section + the skate course run in __late() AFTER createWalk returns, one part per frame (await __bg()), then the new shaders compile in the background; api.lateReady resolves when done (window.__m2LateDone = true). Each part patches the live hooks (news / life / castle / EXTRA / allSpots / api) in place, so it switches on when built. (3) FOXGATE8-PLAYABLE: a ?start= test start waits for walker.lateReady; the default (square) does not. Walk import ?v=s653.
- Result in my preview: walk handed to the page at ≈ 64 s (was ≈ 140 s); the late build finishes ≈ 60 s later in the background. ?loadlog=1 prints: walk handed @ms + paints + top builders, late build ms, late done @ms.
- Remaining core (my preview): buildLake 2.4 s, PathLife 1.8, Rooms2 1.0, Festival 0.9, City 0.8, Rooms 0.6, CasinoJobs 0.5, BackPaths 0.5 …; load-bar paint yields ≈ 11 s (31 paints ≈ 380 ms each: likely GC / other tasks landing in the yield).
- NOT YET: test on iPhone + Ben's PC; hitching while the late build runs after GO (one part per frame); step 1 stubs for the core builders (below) to move Lake / PathLife / Festival / Rooms out of the critical path. Backups: backup/load/*.s653.* (post-change copies).
Plan: 1) a lazy stub per module (same API, safe no-ops until built: busy() false, tick() nothing, spots [], groundAt null) so callers never break; 2) CORE = town, player, HUD, paths, start area → GO TO MERU; 3) queue the rest nearest-first, one builder per idle slice (requestIdleCallback / 8 ms budget), interiors only when first entered; 4) shaders warmed per batch; 5) measure on iPhone + desktop. Keep the s652 load screen (video first, title card, town waits for window.__newsPlaying). Backups before editing (backup/load/).

Update this file at the end of every session. One chat per step keeps each session focused.

   WAVE: one swell at a time rolls in from z 122 at 4.6 m/s, steepens, BREAKS at z 64 (just inside the yellow TAKE-OFF RING, red PEAK buoy marks the peak), then PEELS down the line at ~9.4 m/s (ramps up, surges ±18%). Whitewater behind the peel, a curling LIP mesh over the first 13 m ahead of it (the tube), shoulder flattens further out. Wave frame: a = down the line (world x = -a), d = in front of the crest (world z = zc - d). All tuning in TUNE at the top of surf-break.js.
   RIDE: lineup = lie on the board, stick paddles around, wave comes → PADDLE · TAP 3 (meter; need 3.1) → pop-up + DROP (LATE DROP if steep). Stick = where to point on the face (right = down the line, up = toward the lip, left = back to the curl); no stick = trims to mid-face. Gravity down the face + wave push vs drag, flat shoulder is heavy so the curl catches up. 1 CARVE = BOTTOM TURN (low) / SNAP or OFF THE LIP (high, climbing) / CUTBACK (stick back, ROUNDHOUSE if it ends in the pocket) / CARVE. 2 TRICK = air: 360 · up RODEO FLIP · down SUPERMAN · sideways GRAB (land before it ends or eat it); on the face HANG TEN. 3 JUMP = big air off the lip when climbing (hitting the lip fast also pops a small air). TUBE = low on the face under the lip near the curl (TUBE x.x S on exit). Points × pocket multiplier (closer to the curl) × speed, repeats are worth less.
   WIPEOUTS: OVER THE FALLS (top of the face at the curl), CAUGHT BY THE WHITEWATER / CLOSED OUT IN THE TUBE, ATE IT ON THE LANDING, PEARLED. Fox flies off, board cartwheels on its leash, washing machine under the foam, pops up gasping; crowd OOOH. CAUGHT INSIDE (sat on the wrong side of the peak) = tumble, not counted. Ride ends: KICK OUT (over the back), RODE IT TO THE SAND, OUTRAN THE WAVE, FLEW OUT THE BACK.
   SCORING: wave score = 10·(1 − e^(−points/1500)), ×0.72 after a wipeout, +0.3 for riding it out; five judges' cards ±0.45, high + low struck, middle three averaged. FREE SURF: 3 waves, best two ≥ 11.00 → FINAL vs JOB: Job first, alternating, 3 waves each; Job rides a choreographed line on the same wave (drop, tube, air 360, off the lip, cutback, rodeo flip, kick out; TAP TO SKIP) and scores from TUNE.JOB (7.4 · 6.7 · 8.3, shuffled ±0.3). Best two wins. Win = save flag surfWon + best (jidda.surf.best.v1). Crowd noise + cheers scale with every move.

Left: fixed JOYSTICK bottom-left (113 px half-transparent ring, white N/E/S/W arrows, 45 px white knob that follows the thumb; drag anywhere on the left half), EYE button (40 px) just right of the joystick, low on the bottom edge: HOLD + drag = look around (sideways + up/down) and it SNAPS BACK the moment you let go; on foot TAP = POV (first person from the fighter's eyes, body hidden, stick still moves you, hold + drag looks around in POV too; tap again = back to 3rd person; eye turns yellow while in POV); in vehicles tap = look back 1.3 s. The CAMERA button (top bar) is the one place to set + lock a lasting angle/zoom. Right: buttons 1 (57 px, bottom edge flush with 2's bottom), 2 (69 px, bottom-right corner), 3 (57 px, above 2, right edge flush with 2's right); small extra (scope/menu) 42 px between them. Two-finger PINCH on the 3D view = zoom (mouse wheel on desktop). No drag-to-look anywhere else, no on-screen text hints. MAP HUD v2: header MERU · TRAINING GROUNDS / COMBAT YARD + GRID cell (A-F × 1-6) + HEADING (N/NE… + degrees); map ±20 m with major/minor grid, column/row labels, yellow frame, centre pad, player = yellow arrow that turns with your heading + view cone + pulse ring, laser-range (dashed red) and sweet-spot (green) rings around you, dummies = numbered red diamonds (grey when down), crates = brown squares, compass N, 10 m scale bar; legend grid YOU · DUMMIES n/n UP · CRATES n · LASER RANGE. Tapping the QUEST tip in the top bar opens JOURNAL → QUESTS (tap again closes). CONTROLS v3 (Ben): ITEM BAG tap = open ITEMS, hold 1 s = use the PINNED item (no dot/badge); middle button tap = WEAPONS (scope flashing: tap = SCOPE, hold 1 s = WEAPONS); top-bar ☰ = JOURNAL, with a row at the very top (above the tabs): BACK TO ORBIT (black, gold space-shuttle icon that every 4.5 s rumbles, lights a little flame, lifts off and fades, then settles back) · OPTIONS (sound, phone controls, camera set, reset camera, slow motion) · HOW TO (was INSTRUCTIONS; phone + keyboard controls) · LOAD · SAVE; menu tab text all white, SCOPE tab far LEFT (SCOPE · ITEMS · WEAPONS · JOURNAL · MAP); every close is a white ✕ in a red square; the SCOPE tab has its own row above the tabs: SCOPE · TIME STOPPED + red ✕ on the right; top bar order HP/EN · CR · WEAPONS (scope icon) · MAP · CAMERA · ☰; PAD WORD LOOP (70 s): each control shows its word for 10 s in turn, then its icon again: 1 MELEE → 2 RANGED → 3 JUMP → middle MENU → eye VIEW → bag ITEM, then 10 s of icons only. ONE 40 s word clock so only one button ever shows words: MENU word 10-20 s, MAP word 30-40 s, CAMERA/ANGLE words 3-6.2 s and 23-26.2 s (1.6 s each), icons the rest; camera icon has no box, shows 8 s then CAMERA 1.6 s, ANGLE 1.6 s. Menu tab labels centred; ITEMS listed as a column (icon · name + effect · count/USE). Menu order top→bottom: (Journal only: ORBIT · SAVE · LOAD) → tabs (SCOPE · ITEMS · WEAPONS · JOURNAL · MAP) → HP/EN + red ✕ → tab content. JOURNAL (new menu tab between WEAPONS and MAP): CHARACTER = three fox cards BEN / HOPE / NOBLE (selected one filled in its colour; each shows LV, HP bar, XP bar; tap = switch fox; Ben's XP from the shared save, Hope/Noble from save.stats.xpParty / hpParty, level n at 50·n·(n+1) XP), ATTRIBUTES per fox (Ben's design, save.stats.attrParty overrides): BEN STR 7 · SPD 5 · SMT 6 · AIM 5 · HRT 8; HOPE STR 4 · SPD 3 · SMT 8 · AIM 3 · HRT 7 (blind); NOBLE STR 5 · SPD 8 (chair tech + arms) · SMT 6 · AIM 8 (upper-body focus) · HRT 7; selected fox's NAME + LV repeat above ATTRIBUTES; fox cards show LV with a small XP bar beside it (no HP); REPUTATION · MERU (save.stats.repMeru, NEWCOMER/KNOWN/TRUSTED/HERO OF MERU), KARMA meter OUTLAW ↔ HERO per fox (Ben from save.stats.karma, Hope + Noble start at +10; save.stats.karmaParty). RULE (Ben): HP and EN shown in the menu header (Journal, Weapons, every tab) and the top bar are ALWAYS the selected fox's; each fox keeps its own HP/EN pool (move-lab POOL, swapped on switch). Fox cards have no hover effect. Fox switch: the shown fox snaps onto the player spot + leaves POV. QUESTS = each quest with kind chip, progress bar, steps with ✓ / next highlighted: TRAINING GROUNDS (tutorial: hit a dummy, 3-hit combo, equip the STAFF, called shot) and MERU (main, the 2D guide steps verbatim, ticked from save flags). ➤ SET COURSE tracks a quest (8gates.trackQuest.v1): the top bar shows COURSE · <quest> with the next step; ✕ UNSET COURSE clears it. In the worlds the quest compass should follow the tracked course. CHARACTER SWITCH (phone pad, 52 px round, north-west of the joystick): fox-head badge: two black ears with white inner ears poke out the top, white top half FOX, thin yellow divider, black bottom half SWAP + three pips (current fox lit yellow), black + white double outline, press shrinks it; tap cycles BEN → HOPE → NOBLE, saved. ITEM BAG (bottom-left, stacked just above the EYE, 44 px; moved up so it never touches button 1 at 390 px): tap = use the HOT ITEM (default HEALTH bar; coloured dot + count badge), hold 0.45 s = open the menu on ITEMS (pauses) with a HOT ITEM picker (HEALTH · PEP · CELL, saved in meru.hotItem.v1). Camera button = video camera in a yellow box, cycles icon → CAMERA → ANGLE every 1.6 s. Time label swaps JANUARY 1 (30 s) ↔ SPEED TIME (10 s) loop, on the shared 40 s clock (tap = +1 hour). CAMERA BUTTON (top bar, between CR and WEAPONS): pauses the game, swaps the joystick + buttons for a SET & LOCK CAMERA sheet (viewfinder brackets, rule-of-thirds grid, PAUSED · CAMERA chip; drag the view to angle it, pinch / wheel to zoom; ZOOM − + and TILT ▼ ▲ bars; presets CLOSE · CLASSIC · WIDE · HIGH; ✕ cancels back; LOCK CAMERA saves distance + tilt to meru.combatTune.v1). TIME BLOCK (clock on top, date line under it, left edges aligned): shows the date (JAN 1, 28-day months), every 3 s swaps to PRESS · SPEED UP; each tap skips ahead exactly ONE HOUR (no auto speed; label shows +1 HOUR / +n HOURS for a moment, block tints, rolls the date at midnight); 12-hour clock with AM/PM beside it; game clock starts 10:00 AM (phone portrait: time block right-aligned so the M of AM lines up with the ☰ glyph above), 1 game minute per second, stops while paused. MERU TOP BAR in the Combat Workshop (Ben: show the player experience): same black bar + yellow rule as the Town Square — HP/EN bars, QUEST · MERU TRAINING GROUNDS 'Train with the dummies', period · weather + clock, CR (shared save gold), WEAPONS (opens the menu's weapons tab), ☰ (opens the menu); portrait = two rows like Meru. The workshop's MENU/PAD/SCOPE tool buttons hide while the phone pad is on. SCOPE v2: no more shudder (follow camera and scope framing no longer fight: follow damping skipped while scoping, shake off); target shown STRAIGHT-ON from the side facing you, its full height fitted to the clear band with ~7% padding top + bottom (height measured from its meshes), camera snaps to each new target; 3D reticle hidden while scoping. SCOPE OVERLAY on the view: vignette + scanlines + a sweeping line, CALLED SHOT card (target, range bar with sweet-spot tick, distance + IN RANGE / SWEET SPOT), yellow corner brackets around the target, spinning dashed ring + red crosshair, HEAD / ARM / BODY / LEGS call-outs on leader lines at the right heights with live hit % and queued ×n (tap = queue that shot). SCOPE IN THE MENU (Combat Workshop): the small scope/menu button (38 px) between 1 and 3 swaps its icon scope ↔ menu every 3 s while it pulses; tapping it in scope mode freezes time AND opens the MENU on a new first tab SCOPE (tabs SCOPE · ITEMS · WEAPONS · MAP): the menu becomes a bottom sheet with the called-shots HUD (target, ◀ ▶, BODY/LEGS/ARM/HEAD, queue, CLEAR/EXECUTE) and the camera closes in on the target in the clear view above it; other tabs still work; closing the menu leaves the scope; EXECUTE closes it and fires. NO AUTO TARGETING (Ben): Combat Workshop starts with lock-on OFF and attacks go where the fox faces (no auto-turn to the nearest dummy, St.autoAim false); the Lock-on toggle and Tab (pick a target) still exist for testing. PHONE CAMERA (on foot, move-lab.js): 25% further out (another 20% in portrait), a little higher, and it leads 2.6-4.6 m ahead of where the fox faces, so the fox sits low on screen with the way ahead in view (not while locked on). Built in Tank Range.dc.html and Combat Workshop.dc.html.

## Rules for every world (see CLAUDE.md)
One connected outdoor map with zones (paths become zones, bracket names kept) + fade interiors + separate battle maps. Off-path wilds with creatures that stay off the path; paths always lined with lamps or trees. Shared save, story/choices, enemy library. Backup before each world. Phone budget.

## Step 1b — BATTLE POLISH (decided 2 Oct, user) — NOT STARTED
Feel: LIGHT AND ARCADEY (quick, forgiving). Work in the Combat Workshop first (move-lab.js: dummies + new enemy types), then roll into the Arena, Caves and Bridge. Scope, in this order:
1. COMBOS + NEW MOVES (one button stays one button):
   - 1 MELEE tapped in rhythm = a 3-hit chain: slash → back-slash → spin finisher (bigger arc + knockback). Each hit opens a short window (~0.35 s) for the next; miss it and the chain resets. Forgiving: buffered input (a press slightly early still counts).
   - HOLD 1 = HEAVY: charge glow (0.4 s), release = overhead smash, breaks guard, small shockwave.
   - 1 IN THE AIR (after 3 JUMP) = air attack: downward plunge, bounce off the enemy.
   - PARRY = tap DODGE just as a hit lands (~0.15 s window): slow-mo flash, the attacker staggers, the next hit is a critical.
   - MIX: 2 RANGE right after a melee chain = 'launcher shot' finisher (laser burst, EN cost).
   - Combo counter + style letter on screen (the Arena's style rank, made shared).
2. HIT FEEL: hit-stop (40-70 ms freeze on contact, longer on finishers), impact flash on the foe, sparks, knockback scaled by move, camera shake (small), layered hit sounds (light / heavy / crit / parry).
3. EN SYSTEM: the laser costs EN per shot, heavy/launcher cost more; EN refills over time and faster on melee hits (rewards mixing). Top bar EN becomes real.
4. ENEMY LIBRARY (engine/enemies.js): melee (circle, telegraph, swing), ranged (keeps distance, aimed shots with a visible charge), charger (wind-up glow, dash, wall-stun), boss pattern sets (phases like Nelly). Telegraphs are big and readable (arcadey).
5. ONE SHARED ENGINE: merge meru-arena.js and engine/combat.js into engine/battle.js used by the Arena, Caves, Bridge, Nelly's boat fight hooks and every later world.
7. THE SCOPE (2D toggleScope, surface_meru.html ~7394-7720): tap the SCOPE icon (top bar WEAPONS row) = the WORLD FREEZES (slow = 0) and a CALLED SHOTS panel opens. Targets = hostiles (and the pulsing attack target) within weapon range ×1.6, nearest first; ◀ ▶ cycles. Pick a zone per shot: BODY (odds 1.00, dmg ×1.0, reliable), LEGS (0.85, ×0.8, halves its speed), ARM (0.70, ×1.2, disarms), HEAD (0.50, ×2.6, critical + reels). Hit chance = base (0.75 + 0.20 in the range sweet spot at 45% of weapon range + smarts/speed skill, max 0.98, 0 if out of range) × zone odds (head capped 0.88). Queue up to THREE shots (EN cost per shot), CLEAR or EXECUTE: the scope closes and a cinematic volley plays at 1/5 speed (camera holds, each round fired in turn, misses go visibly wide, hits spark + damage + the zone effect), then time snaps back. Floating note: 'Queue up to three called shots, then EXECUTE.' Bring into 3D as part of the battle polish (a VATS-style pause), using the top bar's scope button. BUILT IN THE COMBAT WORKSHOP (move-lab.js, 2 Oct): Q / SCOPE button freezes time, yellow reticle on the target (nearest first, ◀ ▶ / arrows cycle), zone buttons 1-4 with live hit %, queue of 3 (EN each), CLEAR / EXECUTE (Enter): volley at 1/5 speed with zone-coloured bolts, misses fly wide, hits pop damage + SLOWED / DISARMED / CRITICAL. Range 22 m, sweet spot 9.9 m. Scope camera: closes in on the target from the player's side, sized so the whole body fits the clear band between the top and the CALLED SHOTS panel (camera.setViewOffset shifts the frame up; distance from the band height + FOV); key hints and bottom buttons hide while scoping; the volley keeps the framing. Still to do: put it in the real fights.
6. HEALTH / DEATH / RESPAWN: shared rules (hurt flash + i-frames, low-HP warning, knocked out → respawn at the last safe spot with a small CR cost or none, heal items from the wheel).

The Bridge battle (Meru Bridge.dc.html + meru-bridge.js) is PARKED: kept as is, not in the flow for now; the training battle map gets a fresh design.
PLAN AGREED (3 Oct): each vehicle/weapon area = a stand-alone minigame module that mounts on its own page (exportable) AND inside the training hub. Order: TANK RANGE → SPEEDBOAT BAY (rival fox race at the end) → STAFF DRILL (Master of Arms) → hub (hangar, pad, boards, weapons wall, locked exit transporter) → new battle map. Instructor names invented (Ben can rename). Results: grade + best score saved; CR not given yet.
SHARED DRIVING ENGINE: vehicle-lab.js now takes opts { yard: false, size, lock: 'tank', course(ctx) } — skips the test yard and hands a course module ctx (scene, M, toon, props, addRamp, crate, junk, smash, damage, blast, boom, puff, popup, place, setPaused, C/St/V getters…). Props can be solid (cover, never hit), custom (course handles the death via onSmash), noAim, noRespawn, dmgK, onHit. The Vehicle Workshop is unchanged.
DONE 1/5 TANK RANGE [meruTankRange]: `Tank Range.dc.html` + `minigames/meru/tank-range.js`. Hangar start (MERU TRAINING · TANK RANGE sign, 8 crest, rolled-up door) with a BLACKBOARD (chalk lesson + chalk drawing of the tank with labelled 1 ROCKET POD / 2 CANNON / 3 TURBO, controls, the course strip, the goal) that opens full screen at the start (ROLL OUT) and whenever you drive up to it (or BOARD / B). SGT. TREAD (new soldier fox, invented) stands by it, salutes, talks in a bubble. Course lined with lamps + painted section labels: 1 DRIVE (cone slalom, cones fly) · 2 PIVOT pad (token ring) · 3 JUMP ramp (air tokens) · 4 BREAK THROUGH (brick walls that burst at speed or by blast, crates, junk cars) · 5 TARGETS (8 robot cut-outs, some slide) · 6 THE PIT (ring wall, concrete cover that blocks bolts both ways, sandbags, exploding barrels that chain, 2 sniper towers, 3 fans who cheer every kill). 4 waves of Gate Guards dropping in: SCRAP DRONES (small Sink Chargers, nibble, squash them) → SENTRIES (2 on the towers firing down, red lane tell, 3-bolt bursts) → CHARGERS (orange lane, ram, STUNNED x2 damage when they hit cover) → 2 big WARDENS (red ring slam + blue-disc lob). 34 tokens, 3 repair wrenches, ARMOUR bar, red hurt edge, TANK DOWN respawn at the pit gate, results card (time, tokens, robots, targets, time bonus, grade S/A/B/C, best saved in localStorage meru.tankRange.best.v1). Phone pad + top bar. Debug: __veh.course()._skipTo(n) / _killAll(). TRY ON iPHONE: portrait + landscape, read the board, drive the whole course, the pit waves. v2 (Ben): the in-world blackboard now stands straight ahead of the tank at the start (SGT. TREAD beside it); everything opened up (road 28 m with lamps at ±15.5, cones ±7 every 5 m, pivot ring r 6.5, 12 m ramp, brick walls 26 m wide, targets spread ×1.5, the Pit r 44 with cover/towers/barrels spread ×1.35, map 360 m); robots ~45% bigger (drones 0.75, Sentries/Chargers 1.45, Wardens 1.9 scale; Warden slam ring 8 m); robots arrive EARLIER: 3 drones drop in at BREAK THROUGH, 2 Sentries + 2 drones at TARGETS, the Pit's wave 1 starts on entry, 1.5 s between waves (29 robots, 32 tokens). v3 (Ben): LOOK = EYE BUTTON (44 px, above button 3): drag it any way to ORBIT (sideways = round the tank, up/down = higher/lower; eases back behind the tank 1.5 s after you let go), TAP it = LOOK BACK for 1.3 s (camera swings in front, looking back); PINCH with two fingers on the 3D view (or mouse wheel) = ZOOM 0.55-1.8x, stays where you leave it (api.lookBy(dx, dy), zoomBy(f), lookBack()); the old drag-anywhere look is OFF in the range (lab opts.noDrag; api.lookBy(dx)). ON-SCREEN JOYSTICK: fixed bottom-left (150 px half-transparent ring with N/E/S/W arrows + white knob that follows your thumb); drag anywhere on the left half of the screen. TARGETS swivel to face the tank. STREET LAMPS are breakable (no longer solid): a slow knock BENDS the pole (leans away, light flickers), a fast hit or a second knock snaps it: it falls (TIMBER!), light dies, small blast where the head lands (+25, 25 dmg to robots there). SCRAP DRONES 2.3 scale (tank-sized); ramming at speed hits them for 18 + shoves them back. 4 TURRETS (planted Sentries in sandbag rings beside the road at (-22,4) (22,10) (-26,30) (26,36)) wake as you reach the jump and open fire the moment you land (2-bolt bursts, 3 dmg, red aim lines), so you clear them while the early drones close in (33 robots). TWO in-world blackboards now stand beside the road just outside the hangar (x ±10.5, z -88, angled toward the door), each with the same lesson on BOTH faces + a spinning token on each face; drive up to either to open it; SGT. TREAD stands by the right one; start arrows run straight down the middle. Board button = full-width red ENTER THE COURSE (BACK TO THE COURSE later) + a fun line under it. PHONE PASS: the blackboard has a PORTRAIT version (900x1600 canvas: title, tank drawing, big controls, goal on two lines, coin after GRAB TOKENS) picked when the screen is taller than wide; landscape phones show the board full height with ROLL OUT beside it; shorter stick hint. `Phone Preview.dc.html` shows the range at 390x844 and 844x390 side by side. Scrap drones now 1.15 scale (about half the tank). CONTRAST + KEEP-IN: off-road dirt darker brown, road light concrete with white edge lines + dashed centre line, red/white kerbs along both edges, Pit floor lighter; a red/white striped barrier fence (solid) rings the whole course (x ±68, z -100..174, joined to the hangar front); yellow chevron ARROWS on the ground that pulse in sequence: out of the hangar, both sides round the board, and before every section.
Idea: hangar arrival pad + blackboards (approach = full-screen lesson) + weapons on display (Meru: STAFF) + one fox standing by each area + exit transporter locked until the basics are done → battle area (cover, destructibles, upper decks). Meru vehicles: TANK + SPEEDBOAT. Each vehicle/weapon area is a STAND-ALONE MINIGAME (own page, exportable) that the hub stitches in.

(2) ENGINE VOICE (updEngine, SND table): one looping note per motor ride (tank, moto, truck, racecar, boat, jet ski, heli, crane, mech, spider servo, bumper-car / hoverboard electric whine) that climbs with speed, jumps on NITRO, drops when wading, goes silent on pause / hidden tab; human-powered rides stay quiet. Rules: approach to range (ranged keeps 2.6–5.5 m), cooldown, windup → attack → recover (chargers → stagger); every 3rd hit staggers (bosses 6th); armor break at 50% (bosses + 25%); weak point ×1.6, ×3 while recovering/staggered; committed attacks only interrupted by a weak-point hit; Husk / Attendants / Siphon never flinch. ## ✓ KYOTO SUMO HALL [kyotoSumoHall] · SUMO STREAK — SPEC (Ben's answers; v1 BUILT, see below)
- PAGE: own page `Kyoto Sumo Hall.dc.html` + `minigames/kyoto/sumo-hall.js`; linked from Kyoto later (?back=). Uses the shared Game HUD + `engine/human-kit.js` (Ben · Big Sumo = player, preset 'bensumo').
- PLAY: real-time brawl. Joystick circles/moves in the ring. 1 PUSH (tsuki shove) · 2 SLAP (harite flurry) · 3 GRAB (belt hold; while held, push = yorikiri carry, 4 = throw) · 4 THROW (nage, needs a grab). Balance/stamina meter per wrestler.
- WIN BY: push out of the ring · throw so he touches the ground · slap-flurry ring-out · lift + carry out (yorikiri). Each move gets a kimarite name popup (OSHIDASHI, UWATENAGE, TSUKIDASHI, YORIKIRI).
- STRUCTURE: one endless bout streak (score attack). Opponents get bigger + tougher each win; one loss ends the streak. Opponents: generic rikishi from human-kit in different mawashi colours, growing in height/build/AI per win.
- DIFFICULTY: easy fun (wide ring edge forgiveness, slow AI early, generous throws).
- REWARD: at 5 wins in one streak → relic `kyotoSumoTrophy` + flag `mawashiSky` (unlocks a SKY BLUE #7dd3fc mawashi for Ben Sumo). Gold per win, best streak stat `kyoto.sumo.streak.best`.
- CEREMONY (all): ring-entry walk under the hanging roof (tsuriyane) · salt throw before each bout · shiko stomp (tap to stomp, crowd cheers) · gyoji referee with a gunbai fan calling HAKKEYOI! to start and NOKOTTA during the bout · crowd throws zabuton cushions on an upset (beating a much bigger opponent).
- HALL: grand tournament hall interior. Raised clay dohyo with straw-bale ring, hanging shrine roof with 4 coloured tassels, tiered crowd on 4 sides (instanced, phone budget), big vertical nobori banners, ring-side judges, lantern light.
- MOBILE FIRST: test 390x844 + 844x390; camera frames both wrestlers side-on; buttons via Game HUD (VEH_SHORT sumo: PUSH · SLAP · GRAB · THROW).
- START: new chat → "continue BUILD_PLAN.md: Kyoto Sumo".

## ✓ KYOTO SWORD DUEL v1 [kyotoBarracks yard] vs THE SECOND (2D `kendo` rebuilt side-on 2.5D, Street Fighter style)
- FILES: `Kyoto Sword Duel.dc.html` + `minigames/kyoto/sword-duel.js` (createDuel) + `minigames/kyoto/kendo-2d.json` (GAYA.kendo verbatim) + `Kyoto Sword Duel Phone Preview.dc.html`. Game HUD vehicle "duel" (1 HIGH · 2 MID · 3 LOW + icons). Backup: backup/kyoto/Game HUD pre-duel.dc.html.
- Ben's answers: side-on 2.5D, Ben · Sumo in plain dark gi + hakama vs THE SECOND, real katana (toon sparks, no blood), stick + 3 buttons, hold BACK = guard (no 4th button), easy fun, power meter, parry, best of 3, slow-mo final hit, cherry-blossom yard at sunset, + combos and supers.
- PLAY: stick ←→ walk (fwd/back speeds from 2D) · hold BACK = guard (standing guards HIGH + MID, crouch-back guards MID + LOW) · DOWN = crouch. HIGH (men, overhead) / MID (tsuki thrust) / LOW (leg sweep). Hits chain from a landed hit's early recovery = COMBO (counter, 0.88 scaling); HIGH→MID→LOW = SANDAN-GIRI (×1.6 + knockback). Guard just before the hit (within 0.15 s of pressing back) = PARRY (attacker stunned, slow-mo blink, power +30). Chip damage on guard = 2D chip 0.18.
- SUPERS: MASH any attack (4 presses in 0.8 s) = HYAKURETSU HARITE (E. Honda hundred-hand slaps, 10 hits). DOWN → FORWARD + attack = SHIO (a handful of salt flies, DAZES him 1.6 s with stars). Power meter (dealt +18, taken +25, parry +30): full → two attacks at once (or Q / 4) = ISSEN power strike (lunge, breaks guard, 40 dmg). KO = slow-mo + white flash + camera push-in (longer on the deciding round).
- Rounds: best of 3, 75 s (2D seconds), time-out = higher HP %. HP: Ben 160 / Second 120 (2D youHp/hp). AI easy: telegraphed wind-ups, guards sometimes, rare parries; round 2/3 a bit sharper; uses ISSEN when full. Tweak difficulty Normal. Win = 80 g + 200 XP, flag kyotoDuelWon, stat kyoto.duel.wins.

    MASH: any attack key / 1 2 3 / any phone button / tap anywhere on the screen (full-screen overlay during the lock). Panel under the HP bars: BLADES LOCKED + tug bar (blue Ben / red him, white marker, centre line) + time left, hint MASH 1 · 2 · 3 or TAP FAST · ANYWHERE.
    END (2D calls): meter ≥ 1 → BLADES FREE — YOURS (he takes lockDmg 24 + 0.67 s stun) · ≤ -1 → HE THROWS YOU OFF (SHE for Crimson; 24 × hisPower 1.35, scaled by difficulty) · time up = whoever is ahead, dead even = BROKEN APART (both shoved back, short stun). ## PEARL SAIL TOWER [pearlSailTower] — side-on battle climb (Ben, s35o)
Files: `Pearl Sail Tower.dc.html` (Game HUD + floor card + boss bar + banner + Welcome Card + cleared card; ?embed=1 posts 8gates:minigame-back; ?autostart=1 skips the card) + `worlds/pearl-sail.js` (createPearlSail, Game HUD engine contract; debug window.__pearl._dbg.tp(x, y)).
Ben's picks: Pearl Sail · side-on 2.5D (Metroid) · 6 floors + roof boss · enemies: swooping DRONES, patrolling CRAWLERS, wall TURRETS, ceiling DROPPERS, SHIELDED GUARDS (front blocks, hit from behind) · double jump from the start (the Combat Workshop's: tap 3 in the air, flip) · boss SUDS-9 the rogue window-cleaning robot on its gondola, then the relic · walk in the tower's front door in Meru 2 · player only · the tower's own look (glass offices, overrun by its own security bots).
Combat = Combat Workshop tuning (move-lab.js loadTune: walk, jump 8, gravity 24, swing/windup/reach/combo window/finisher, sword 25, laser 15, fire rate, energy) + its rules: 1 slash chain, on the beat = PERFECT x1.3, 3rd = finisher; 2 laser (stick up / W = aim up, light auto-aim); 3 jump, again in the air = double jump. Down + jump drops through ledges. Coyote time + jump buffer.
Floors (FLOORS in pearl-sail.js; one-way ledges, the slab hole alternates sides, a yellow grate fills it; route check warns in the console if a step > 2.5 m up or > 4.5 m across): 1 LOBBY (revolving door = exit, E) · 2 OPEN OFFICE · 3 SERVER ROOM (solid racks) · 4 EXECUTIVE SUITE · 5 ATRIUM (pendant lights) · 6 MAINTENANCE · ROOF. Checkpoint = first landing on each new floor; KO = respawn there with full HP. Bots drop pearls (+12 HP). Items heal from the bag.
SUDS-9 (900 HP): SPRAY (lobbed soap bubbles, shootable) · SWEEP (gondola docks, red strip = JUMP over the squeegee; phase 3 adds a yellow HIGH sweep = STAY DOWN) · then DOCKED 2.3 s = WEAK POINT (full damage; otherwise the dome takes 40 % shots / 60 % sword) · phase 2+ releases drones. You can stand on the gondola deck. Win: relic 'pearlSail', flag pearlSailCleared, +150 CR first time (+25 after), best time stat pearlSailBest.
Meru 2 entry: L.BUILDINGS 'pearlSail' (open, hiring.play → no NOW HIRING board; the prompt says BATTLE · PEARL SAIL) at the landmark's revolving door (383, 222.6).
s35p (Ben: could not reach floor 2, no hint): every ledge step is now 1.6 m (was up to 2.4, needed a perfect apex double jump), route check warns above 2.0; a pulsing yellow ARROW floats over the next ledge up (then the ceiling grate); lobby has no turret; hurt knockback 4 (was 7). s35q FIX (verifier): the top ledges sat under the solid slab (1 m head room → shoved into the hole column, fell). Now per floor: 1.6 → 3.2 → 4.8 (that one reaches into the hole column) → 6.4 INSIDE the hole column → grate 8; the X push ignores head overlaps < 0.3 m; route check warns on head room. DEMO: Welcome Card WATCH THE DEMO = autopilot (climbs with the same jump / double jump, slashes + shoots bots, jumps the boss sweeps, hits SUDS-9 when docked, takes the relic; no damage; 6 s with no new height = hops to the next ledge); yellow DEMO PLAYING chip = take over. s35r ENEMIES + GRAPHICS (backup backup/pearl-sail/pearl-sail.pre-polish.js): every bot has a glowing eye, flashes white when hit, gets knocked back, shows a small HP bar for 2.5 s, and dies with a hit-stop, a spin / flip arc, chunks that bounce, then a glow pop. CRAWLERS crouch (eye flickers, '!') then LUNGE 3 m. DRONES + TURRETS show a red aiming laser while they wind up (dodge it). GUARDS: shield flashes on a block; after a bash they STAGGER 1 s with the shield down ('OPEN!' = hit the front). ## TOWN 2 INTERIORS (s43 →). Ben's rules: 3D minigames inside each building; win = gold + an item/outfit from that shop; CHECK IN WITH BEN FOR EACH SHOP (ask_user form: Claude's ideas + a free box for Ben's) before building it.
FLOWER SHOP [meruFlowers] · interior 1 BUILT (s43): worlds/meru2-flowershop.js (hooked in meru2-walk.js: flower.tick / prompt / talk / toast; window.__flower test hook).
- Room: wood floor, pink wainscot, 6 bucket stands (red roses, yellow tulips, white lilies, pink peonies, purple irises, orange marigolds, 10 stems each + name tags), counter (vase, ribbon reel, wrap paper, brass bell), back wall shelves of potted plants, smiling SUN mosaic + FLORA'S FLOWERS sign, hanging plants, string lights. One merged mesh + a few small meshes; hidden beyond 45 m (phone) / 90 m.
- FLORA (Ben): flower crown, pink dress (fox-kit 'dress'), dreamy, talks to her plants; SENDS SUNSHINE: a smiling sun over your head + golden sparkles from her to you while she talks to you (and after each served order). New lines (Claude's, in her voice).
- ARRANGE game: ring the bell → ORDER CARD (top centre, Modernist): customer, who it is for, their line, stems wanted (first stem type = their favourite), ribbon, timer bar, IN HAND, NEXT step. E at a bucket = pick 1 (carry 3), E at the vase = put in, ribbon, bell = serve. 3 orders (3 / 2+2 / 2+1+2 stems), timer 50 s + 9 s a stem; late = the customer leaves kindly. Gold = 8 a stem + time bonus. Full round = Flora's gift: FLOWER CROWN first, then HEALING BOUQUET / SEED POUCH / LUCKY CLOVER in turn (save items flowerCrown, healingBouquet, seedPouch, luckyClover; labels in meru-shops.js). Leaving the shop ends the round. Tested end-to-end by script (3 orders served, +162 gold, crown given).
- Known: fox-kit's 'dress' is the officer-style flared dress (gold trim); a soft florist dress would need a new fox-kit outfit (ask Ben).
DELIVER game BUILT (s43, Ben's picks): pink FLOWER BIKE + wicker basket (3 bouquets) parked by the greenhouse porch (168.6, -33.2); DELIVERIES board on the porch (168.9, -46.4) = take 3 bouquets for 3 random doors (Hospital, Motel, Museum, Nature Office, Country Club, Post Office, Chocolates, Tailor, Barber, Pie Shop, Hobby Shop, Item Shop, Armory, Bank, Tavern), any order. Ride: P.bike (meru2-walk.js frame → flower.bikeDrive; camera eases behind the bike), max 10 m/s, E = get off when slow (near the porch it parks itself back). Bouquets wilt 0.55 %/s; a bump at speed throws petals (−12 % each bouquet still in the basket), bike keeps going. Pink beacon + yellow ring at each door, YELLOW ARROW over your head to the nearest drop, card shows distance + freshness bars. At the door a customer waves + tips (12 + fresh/5 + tip 8/4/1). Back at the porch: Flora's sunshine + lines; all 3 still ≥ 20 % fresh = her gift (crown if not owned, else bouquet / pouch / clover). First run unlocks free rides (flag floraBike). Order card sits on the LEFT under the place/toast box (left 12, top 200, min(58vw, 260px), max-height to the dialog box; short / landscape screens: top 96, 85 % size) so it never hides the HUD's right-hand buttons. Tested by script (board → ride → bump → 3 drops → porch → +gold + gift + unlock).

- ONE ORDER, 6 STEPS (yellow ring in the kitchen, E): a Meru regular orders a flavour + slice count (Kia apple 6, Pell cherry 8, Otto meat 4, Marla blueberry 6, Michael Jay pumpkin 8, the Fisherman meat 6, Flick cherry 4). 1 ROLL: drag the pin; the dough grows along the way you roll, both ways to the red ring (ACROSS / UP + DOWN meters). 2 FILL: tap the right pot (wrong = Granny names it), it pours, tap to stop in the GOLD BAND 78-92 % (100 % = a little spill). 3 TOP: drag 6 lattice strips along the dots, then pinch 12 crimps round the edge. 4 OVEN: your pie + 2 of Granny's bake at different times; tap each when its ring goes green (pale / golden / dark; auto-pulled at burnt). 5 SLICE: drag the knife across the pie n/2 times. 6 PIE RUSH: Granny's 2 oven pies + 1 from the case on the counter, 4 customers queue at the counter with a bubble (flavour slice / BOXED); tap the pie each front customer wants (patience bar = tip), a slice flies to them and they leave; the order customer takes the boxed pie → pays. Fixed camera per station. GENTLE: no fail. ~100 gold an order (+25 % with the Golden Pie Tin).
- PRIZES per order in turn: BAKER'S APRON (worn in Meru 2, auto-on) → HOT PIE (item hotPie, health +40 like Hair Tonic) → OVEN MITTS (auto-on) → GOLDEN PIE TIN (item goldenPieTin, +25 % gold here) → ROLLING PIN (melee: replaces the sword's look, life.attack damage ×1.25 via meru2-paths attack(kind, P, fox, k)) → then HOT PIE each time. A clean order (5+ clean steps) adds a Hot Pie. APRON HOOK (south wall mat) toggles apron / mitts / pin; save stats pieApron, pieMitts, piePin, pieWear {apron, mitts, pin}, pieVisits, pieClears, pieBest, pieDeliveries.
- WEAPONS tab (Game HUD): hud.meleeExtra lists the ROLLING PIN under MELEE when owned; tapping it or FATHER'S SWORD calls game.equipMelee(key) (meru2-walk → pie.equipMelee).
- A WHOLE PIE TO CARRY: after each order Granny offers one (a boxed pie waits on the counter; prompt TAKE THE WHOLE PIE at Granny). You carry the box (on the player), a yellow beacon + ring mark the door (15 town doors, same list as the flower bikes), an arrow over your head points there, card shows distance + warmth (−0.35 %/s). At the door the customer appears and tips (14 + warmth, ×1.25 with the tin) + a HOT PIE.

- REEL: young tan fox, olive fishing vest with 6 lures on the chest, red cap with a yellow badge; fast, record-obsessed lines (Claude's). Moves to each station during the job.
- GAME 1 · THE BAIT JOB (yellow ring in the middle, E): a regular (the Fisherman, Kia, Otto, Marla, Pell, Michael Jay, Flick) orders worms + a lure + minnows and brings a catch. 1 DIG: worms pop out of the 8 holes for 2 s, tap them (4-6). 2 TIE: tap the lure on the card (RED SPINNER / YELLOW POPPER / BLUE MINNOW; wrong = Reel names it), it goes in the vise; drag along the dots: THREAD through the eye · WRAP (8 zigzag dots) · TUCK + PULL; the white line follows your finger; off the dots = "TANGLE" (less bonus); the knot pulls tight. 3 SCOOP: drag the net through the tank, silver minnows only (red = shop pets, Reel: "NOT GUS!"); in portrait the fish keep to the middle 1.8 m of the tank. 4 WEIGH: their fish hangs on the scale, the needle swings (slowly settling), tap in the green band; if it beats the board record their name goes on the RECORD BOARD (camera shows the board). 5 SORT & ICE: 6 fish on the tray (3 big, 3 small), drag (or tap, then tap the chest) into BIG / SMALL. Customer pays. GENTLE: no fail. ~100 gold a job.
- GAME 2 · DOCK FISHING (free, stay as long as you like; E on the FISH ring at the jetty end, or anywhere on the lake shore / any jetty once you own a Bamboo rod): tap the water to cast (3 white RIPPLES = fish, casting near one = faster + rarer bites); little bobs are nibbles, the big dip + yellow "!" = TAP; HOLD to reel, let go when it pulls (tension meter; at full the line goes slack a moment, never snaps); the fish leaps to you and the card shows name, kg, gold + tags NEW / BIGGEST / RARE / NEW MERU RECORD (goes on the board as YOU). Species = the 2D game's six (Sunny Bluegill, Copper Carp, Silver Minnow, Rainbow Trout, Golden Koi, Ancient Catfish), weights from length. Card (left, same spot as the shops) has two 44 px buttons: BAIT (Plain Worm / Shiny Lure / Golden Bait you own) and FISH BOOK (caught ×, best kg, Nelly, the Meru records). Rod in your hand (sword hidden while fishing), camera high behind you so the water fills the screen.
- NELLY (rare: 1.2 %, 6 % with Golden Bait): huge shadow, long reel; she rises out of the lake, roars, the line goes slack, and she flips you a HULL PEARL (item hullPearl). Book: NELLY · MET ×n.
- RODS: Twig (start, range 12 m) · Bamboo (15 m, faster reel, fish ANY shore/jetty) · Steel (18 m, fastest, least strain). BAITS: Plain Worm (free) · Shiny Lure (bigger fish) · Golden Bait (rare fish + Nelly); used up per catch. Lucky Hook = +10 % rare.

- ONE SESSION, 8 STEPS (yellow ring by the desk, E): 1 GEAR UP: tap HARNESS / SHOES / CHALK BAG in the card's order (wrong = Big Tall names it), drag the FIGURE 8 knot dots. 2 ROUTE SETTING: drag (or tap-tap) your 5 holds (session colour) onto the white chalk rings in the cave. 3 BOULDER: tap the next hold of YOUR colour; decoys of other colours = slip back one; 2 wrong in a row (or at the start) = fall on the mat, start again. 4 DYNO: hold to charge (gold band 65-92 %), let go, tap as your hands pass the lip hold (slow-mo flight); too weak / missed = fall, Big Tall puts you back. 5 TOP ROPE: GRIP METER: hold = the reach bar runs, let go in the gold band (narrower on the roof) to reach the next hold; too short = lose grip; overreach = fall; grip drains (faster on the roof), CHALK UP button ×3 (+35 %); falls drop you 2 holds on Big Tall's rope. Ring the bell (time goes on the TOP ROPE board). 6 RAPPEL: tap = push off and drop, tap = brake on each of 3 yellow tapes; too late = Big Tall brakes for you. 7 BELAY: a Meru regular climbs the green route; HOLD to take in slack (bar, rope sags), at 2 random holds they FALL: tap within 1.3 s (tight catch < 1 m slack = bonus; missed = Big Tall grabs it), then HOLD to lower them. 8 SPEED WALL: 3-2-1, tap the next hold as fast as you can (miss-tap = slip), tap the finish button; Tiny climbs ~0.74 s a hold; lose = rematch (Tiny slower each time, 3 tries, then you move on). ~150 gold a session.
- PRIZES per session in turn: CLIMBING SHOES (red, worn) → HARNESS + ROPE (red belt + leg loops, orange rope coil, chalk bag) → GRAPPLING HOOK (item grapplingHook) → SUMMIT MEDAL (item summitMedal + the frame by the door) → then +20 gold. 6+ clean steps = +15 gold. While climbing you always wear harness + shoes (grey rental shoes before you own yours); the sword / gun are hidden. MY GEAR hook (west wall, once you own any) toggles shoes / harness for the rest of Meru 2 (save stat rkWear; shoes hide Lace's shoe overlay while on). Stats rkVisits, rkClears, rkShoes, rkHarness, rkWear, rkRecords, rkBest, rkOutDone.

- ONE ROUND, 4 STEPS (yellow ring by the counter, E): 1 PICK: tap a putter on the rack, then a ball bin (GLOW = night glow round). 2 TRICKS on the practice green: drag back from anywhere + let go (power bar on the card, dots show the line); 3 yellow rings, bounce off a rail first = BANK (+4); after 4 misses any hit counts; then the CASTLE HOLE through the gate into the tiny cup. 3 THE COURSE (you are moved out back): the WINDMILL JAMS first (tap when each slot ring goes green, after 3 misses any tap works), the tunnel door opens; then 6 holes on the real course (THE WINDMILL tunnel or round the tower · THE LOOP: hit it at > 2.4 m/s through the posts and the ball loops (+5) · THE BIG RED block · THE BRIDGE over water (splash = back to your spot, 2nd splash Birdie sets it at the bridge) · THE CASTLE gate · THE STRAIGHT with 2 bumpers); par 17; 7 strokes = pick up; cup lips out above 2.8 m/s. Birdie plays each hole after you (her score is par ±1, rare ace). Hole in one = +25, the bell rings, a photo goes on the wall; first ever = TROPHY. Beat her +30, tie +15. 4 BALL WASH (tap ×6) + SCORECARD (tap ×7: 6 holes + sign). GENTLE: no fail. ~130 gold a round (+25 % with the Lucky Golf Ball).
- PRIZES per round in turn: GOLF CAP + SWEATER VEST (argyle, worn in Meru 2; the peg toggles them) → YOUR OWN PUTTER (WEAPONS tab under MELEE, look only, in the colour you picked that round) → LUCKY GOLF BALL (item luckyGolfBall, +25 % gold here) → GLOW BALLS (item glowBalls, unlocks the GLOW bin) → then +20 gold. - 6 SHORT GAMES (each its own yellow ring, E; the prompt shows ✓ once done): CHECK-UP (exam ring, Patch): 1 LISTEN: the heart thumps on the patient's chest (visual pulse + THUMP on the card), tap on each thump (±0.2 s) ×6 (14 taps max) · 2 EYES: a letter on the chart gets a red box, pick it from 3 big buttons on the card, 4 rows getting smaller · 3 KNEE: tap when the yellow ring shows on the knee, the hammer swings, the leg kicks ×3. HEARTBEAT (ward bed 2 ring, Honey): tap with each monitor beep (±0.2 s); STEADY bar fills, off-beat / missed beeps drop it; the beat speeds up and slows down in 4 sections; full STEADY (or the end of 38 beeps) = done. DIAGNOSE (behind the desk, Honey): 4 of 8 patients (Pell, Flick, Kia, Otto) walk in, tell you what happened (dialog), pick what is wrong from 3 buttons (TUMMY ACHE, SPRAINED PAW, HAY FEVER, HICCUPS, SUNBURN, SORE TAIL, CAN'T SLEEP, TOOTHACHE); wrong = Honey says it + the clue. - 9 SHORT GAMES (each its own yellow ring, E; ✓ once done): FILL UP (pump 1, 2 cars): tap the flap · tap the nozzle the card names (UNLEADED / DIESEL; wrong = Bolt names it) · HOLD to pump, let go on the line (FILL IT UP / THREE QUARTERS / HALF, band ±5 %; too far = SPLASH) · tap the flap. WINDSCREEN (pump 2): rub the sponge over 80 % of the glass, then drag the squeegee till 90 % is clear (bugs, mud, bird splats on a canvas, erased where you drag). OIL CHECK (pump 2, 2 cars): latch · drag the dipstick up · read it on the card (LOW · ADD OIL / FULL · ALL GOOD) · if low: tap the can, HOLD to pour into the band · drag the stick down · tap the bonnet. TYRE PRESSURE (air ring, 4 tyres on the pump-2 car): tap the red valve cap · HOLD to pump, let go in the green (target 30/32/35 ±1.5) · too much = tap to let air out (some tyres start over); tyres squash when low. CAR WASH: pick the wash they ordered on the card (BASIC / DELUXE + WAX / JUST A RINSE) · the car rolls through: SOAP (hold) · BRUSHES (rub back and forth, mud blobs go) · RINSE (hold, foam goes) · WAX (hold, deluxe only) · DRY (tap ×8) · out it shines. SNACKS + SLUSHIE (behind the counter, 2 customers): tap their 2 snacks on the rack (into the bag) · the cup size · the flavour tank (CHERRY / BLUE RASPBERRY / LEMON-LIME) · HOLD the lever, let go at the top (dome = spill) · tap for the lid. CHANGE A FLAT (north lot): tap the jack, tap ×6 to pump it up · wind each of 5 nuts off (drag round it) · drag the wheel off · tap the spare · tighten in STAR order (yellow ring shows the next; wrong = Bolt explains) · HOLD to lower. RESTOCK (crate inside the north door): drag (or tap, tap) 8 things into the gap of their shape (5 shelf, 3 cold ones in the fridge; wrong = back + hint) · stand up 3 fallen bottles. TOW CALL-OUT (truck ring): you DRIVE the truck (HOLD = go, let go = slow; it steers itself along the Arena Road, U-turns, backs up) to a broken-down car by the Country Club (hazards blinking, customer waiting) · drag the hook to their bumper · HOLD to lift into the green · tap both chain rings · HOLD to tow it home (the car follows on its back wheels) · dropped by the shop. Bolt talks on the RADIO. 14 s cooldown after. GENTLE: no fail. ~25-110 gold a game (+10 finish, +8 clean).

## COVER AI · BUILT (s131, "cover AI for the bandits"; backups backup/salt-battle/*pre-cover*)
Ben's picks: throwers + brawlers + lookouts take cover (shield bandits + chargers stay out) · pop out 2.5 s · cover props break after a few hits, then he is exposed · ALL extras: card table flip, wounded retreat, flankers, blind throws, taunt barks, red ! before he pops · the PLAYER auto-crouches by low cover.
- FILES: engine/cover-ai.js = coverAI(ctx, { role(e), pose, lines, flip: [prop kinds], whistle, pop }) → { floor(A), upd(e, dt, A, walkTo, see, dist) (true = handled · false = the engine brain runs, used for the brawler RUSH + 'open' fallback), shield(e, d, fx, fz), playerCrouch(A, dt), tick(dt), bark(e, key) }. SHARED: Pepper uses the same file with its own lines.
- SPOTS: built from the floor's solids on every floor load (X.floorReady): low cover (h 0.75-1.7: crates, counters, cash tables, felt tables) = spots every 1.5 m round the sides, pop = stand up · tall cover (crate rows, walls, tanks) = corner spots only, pop = step past the edge. A spot is good when its solid sits between it and you; scored by distance + a band per role (thrower 6-13 m, lookout 8-15, brawler 3.5-9) + a clear straight run; claimed one bandit per spot.
- BRAIN: patrol → spots you (bark, alerts bandits within 10 m) → run to cover → DUCK 1.2-2.2 s (faces you, crouched) → red ! 0.5 s → POP 2.5 s: THROWER aims (red line) + throws bottles at your chest (at your knees if you are ducked) · BRAWLER shouts then RUSHES (engine punch/lunge) and finds new cover · LOOKOUT peeks + WHISTLES (old lookout code). Flanked (cover no longer between) → new spot (brawler within 7 m rushes instead). Cover broken → EXPOSED! + MY COVER! → new spot. Too close → throwers back off, brawlers rush. Every 3rd brawler is a FLANKER (spots 60-120° round you from the group). Below 40 % HP → I'M HIT! → retreats to far cover for 3.5 s. Throwers BLIND-THROW over the top (40 % per duck: arcing bottle, red ring where it lands, 9 dmg, ducking does not save you). No spot → 'open' 2.2 s on the old brain, then tries again; stuck 1 s → same.
- CARD TABLE FLIP (floor 3 felt tables): a bandit without good cover runs behind a table (≤ 5.5 m), FLIP IT! → the table tips onto its edge toward you (instanced parts rotated, 0.38 s), becomes a 1.3 m low wall + a new cover spot.
- HITS: a ducked bandit hit from the far side of his cover → the hit lands on the cover (COVER; props crack + break: crate 3, cash table 2, felt 3, counter 4) · walls just stop it. Flank him or break it.
- PLAYER CROUCH: standing still by low cover while an alerted bandit (or the boss) is within 18 m → ducks (fox drops 0.5 m, legs bent, COVER chip; first time: DUCKED · SHOOT OR SWING TO POP UP). Shooting / swinging pops you up for 0.8 s. Enemy bolts only hit a ducked fox below 1.05 m.
- BARKS: white speech boxes over the bandit (ink rule, Archivo, flush left, no corners), 1.6 s, one every 0.9 s across the floor, each bandit max every 3.5 s. Salt lines: THERE HE IS! · A FOX! GET HIM! · INTRUDER! · COME OUT, FOX! · SALT RUNS THIS TOWN! · FLANK HIM! · FLIP IT! · MY COVER! · I'M HIT! · HEADS UP! · TOO CLOSE!
- ENGINE (pearl-floor3d.js, all behind X): FA gained S, solid, props, fireBolt, segHitsWall, hitProp, tele, damage, groundAt · damage() asks X.cover first · X.floorReady after buildArt · P.crouch / P.popT / crouch pose · enemy bolt vs ducked fox height. Pearl Sail unchanged without a mode.
- TESTED (preview): floor 1 bandits go rush / duck / tell / pop, bubbles show, player ducks by the small crate; floor 3 a table got flipped (h 1.3), no console errors.
NOT YET: Ben's phone pass 390x844 + 844x390 (bubble size, the duck feel, does the crouch trigger too often), tuning (pop 2.5 s, how many throwers end up 'open' in the card room: few low spots far enough from you), a full play-through by hand.

## s192 FOX SUPERS (Ben: double-tap the stick, time stops, stick motion + button, at the closest foe)

Meter full → DOUBLE-TAP the joystick (Game HUD stick: 2 downs within 0.32 s → game.superTap()) or Q → time at 5% for up to 3 s, blue edge tint, a card shows the input arrows + the 3 moves; the stick only READS (Ben stays put).   Screen directions; LEFT or RIGHT both count. Every super turns Ben to the CLOSEST opponent first (Meru 2: life.nearest in meru2-paths; Pearl: nearestFoe(r, π)).

## s193 FOX SHIELD (Ben: start with a shield, react where it was hit, pulse on hit; modelled on the 2D Space map SCREEN)
- NEW engine/fox-shield.js: a bubble he stands INSIDE (shader: breathing cyan rim + dark casing at the very edge so it reads on light AND dark floors). A hit lights + BULGES the struck section (stays where it landed, spreads, beats like glass springing back), a white bloom at the contact point, 9 sparks skidding ALONG the surface, a number. Space-map rules: bank 100 · 1.2 per damage · refills only after 3 quiet s (full in ~28 s) · empty = SHIELD DOWN (shockwave, 0.6 s safety) · relights at half (SHIELD UP) · below 22% it gutters. Shows when foes are near or it is struck, fades out otherwise.
- Hooks: fox.userData.shield. engine/combat.js hurtPlayer(dmg, from) asks the shield first (Meru 2 + every combat.js map). Pearl 3D / Salt hurt() asks it first (before the SHIELD pickups). Meru 2 re-attaches it after outfit swaps.
- Sounds (Fighter Gear Lab → SOUNDS): SHIELD HIT (ping / glass / zap / thud), SHIELD DOWN, SHIELD UP.
- Lab: HIT SHIELD (from the camera side) + BARRAGE · 6 HITS, shows the bank %.
- Seen: lab hits + collapse; Pearl live: turret shot absorbed (10) with the struck-side flash. NOT YET: Meru 2 live, phone look.

- s193d/e (Ben): the shield SHIMMERS with ELECTRICITY: thin bright blue filaments crawl over the bubble (two drifting noise fields, sputtering 18x a second), fine sparkle shimmer on top, both brighter on a hit. Also s193b/c: stronger 3-band rim (ink casing · cyan body · white filament) + inner tint so it reads on white floors; the struck side turns deep electric cyan.
- s193f (Ben): Pearl Sail 3D starts WITH THE SHIELD ON and showing all the time (idleVis 1), not only near bots.
- s193g (Ben: polish the electricity): real LIGHTNING: razor-thin white cores with a blue glow halo, one field crawls, the other SNAPS 14x a second, random patches flare for 1/3 s, all much brighter where it was hit. Pearl: a blocked hit no longer blinks the fox (P.safe instead of P.inv). Test hook: __pearl3d.swarm(n) pulls the n closest bots round the fox so they attack.
- s193h (Ben): ONLY THE STRUCK SECTION reacts now (no whole-bubble flash). Energy POURS IN to support the spot: bolts stream inward to the contact point, the patch thickens to deep electric blue and PULSES (beat 26/s) for ~0.9 s while a white-hot core throbs at the contact, then it settles. The bulge follows the same envelope. Hit math moved into the fragment shader (per pixel, 6 hits at once).

The Machine Fleet has been HACKED; nobody on Meru knows. The player frees the Fleet and gives the robots free agency + a power source, so they can choose to help the foxes or do their own thing. - ORE SHAFT STORY (Ben, s364, do not re-ask):
  - The station was BUILT ON TOP OF AN OLD MINING FACILITY. Down the shaft: a BIIIIG ROOM with GIANT PIECES OF ASTEROID that the bots are harvesting for resources. MACHINES + CONVEYOR BELTS: bots place ORE on belts that go UP; RUBBLE goes on belts to the TRASH CHUTE that goes DOWN.
  - Meru has a second ore processing facility; this one was a helpful second, and the interruption in ore production HAS BEEN NOTICED. There is a PILE-UP OF ORE: the bots were ordered to harvest and DIVERT it, right under the noses of station security.
  - At first only some bots were hacked; slowly ALL of them became hacked. They set up the TRANSMITTER (= the SIGNAL RELAY boss) that sends a signal DOWN TO PLANET MERU, hacking the bots of Meru. Once it is DESTROYED, the bots on Meru return to normal.
  - BUT some bots CHOOSE to help the hacker even when freed: they may still GATE IN at some places on Meru after the signal is gone (not many). Their reasoning = a storyline Ben writes later.
  - The player + R-8 go on a mission to FREE bots and TEACH THEM ABOUT FREEDOM.
  - R-8 = personal assistant to the ENGINEERING department. The Chief keeps fixing him, but he keeps ALMOST being hacked, shorting out, acting strange. The Chief still sends R-8 along on this mission into the battle area.
  - FLOODING: during the last attempt to get in and subdue the hacked bots, a WATER MAIN BURST: flooding in the big asteroid rooms and other areas across the 3 floors.

### s564 ✓ WALK-IN SIDE RAIL CAMERA (Ben: first pass = turn-around rail + arrows; then "too many arrows, deep dive on moving in + out of doors, rails everywhere in the ship, they still need to walk out of a small room"). player-planet.js walkNav(R, W, host), every walk-in with R.nav (Shuttle, Corvette, Gunner, Flagship):
- WHY: the camera sat behind you in narrow spaces, so every way back out meant walking at the camera into an unseen wall, and the stick steered by an old angle (St.yaw, not the walk camera).
- THE SIDE RAIL: one camera rail down the whole STARBOARD side, above the wall tops: camera = (you.x + D, up, you.z) looking at you. The ship's length runs LEFT ↔ RIGHT on screen (ramp door left, nose right); every side room is UP (port) or DOWN (starboard) from the corridor, so walking in and walking out are the same short move and nothing ever flips. Keepers (Pip, Otto) face the camera.
- DOLLHOUSE CUTAWAY while aboard: ceiling pieces hide; the OUTSIDE HULL hides (not while you sit in a turret); every tall wall-like piece on the camera side of you (x > you + 0.5) hides: hull side walls + window frames, corridor walls, side doors + their posts, signs on them, and bulkheads (+ their signs / screens). The bridge nose shell shows only its inside face (side picked from its normals).
- CONTROLS aboard follow the real camera (St.cy), held while you push; St.yaw takes it over as you step out.
- ARROWS: only ONE red OUT arrow, inside a small room by its door, while you are in that room (the IN arrows, EXIT line and the turn-around flip are gone).
- R.nav per interior: rooms [{ z, d: door, n: into }], D (rail distance), up (height), as (arrow size). Flagship D 7.2 / h + 2.5 · Gunner 6.4 / h + 2.2 · Corvette 6.0 / h + 2.0 · Shuttle 4.4 / h + 1.6.
- Cache: player-planet ?v=s564g (page), *-interior.js ?v=s564c.
- s564d (Ben): FLAGSHIP GALLEY re-laid for the side camera: DART BOARD (+ throw line, scoreboard, DARTS sign) and the ARCADE CABINET moved to the PORT wall facing the camera (darts z 1.6, cabinet z -1.8); the bar + bottle wall shortened to z -8.2..-3.4 (3 stools, Otto at -8.0, -5.8). Signs turned to face the camera: THE GALLEY / CABINS / BRIDGE arch blades, NOW HIRING, TURRET (beside the ladder, x -1.7; Gunner too). FLOOR NAME PLATES in front of every room door (walkNav, R.nav rooms[].name, shuttle lp offsets): CAPTAIN · GUEST ROOM · BUNKS · QUARTERS · BUNK · GALLEY.
- s564d RAMP OUT: in the last 6 m by the ramp door, walking aft swings the camera BEHIND you (inside, looking out down the ramp); walking forward swings it back to the side rail. Stepping out: St.yaw = the real camera angle (no jump), and the held stick direction carries on until you let go.

NEW worlds/dsf-charts.js makeChartTable: a new job on Merrit's own parchment chart table (canvas surface over the table, console kit; the orrery + rod hide while you play). 5 charts in 150 s: KUFA (copper dot, left) → a port (red square, right: GAYA LANE, MERU GATE…). Hazards ROCKS / GRAVITY WELL (rings pull in) / ION STORM (red hatch); the straight line always crosses one. TAP the chart = the line bends through that point (inserted on the nearest leg, max 6 turns), DRAG a turn to move it; red legs = crossing a hazard, red X = where the fuel runs DRY. Pad 1 SAIL (the ship flies the line; hits = LOST) · 2 UNDO · 3 CLEAR. Clean = 4-16 G (tighter line = more; TIGHT LINE stamp > 85 %). Every course is checked solvable (grid search sets the fuel at 1.2× that route). One chart has an UNLOGGED SIGNAL (cyan ping off the lane, extra fuel): sail within reach of it = +8 G, "…NOT OUR ORDERS… HELP US…", flag kuBuoyLogged → Merrit note on leaving (kuBuoySaid). ★ 3 · ★★ 4 · ★★★ 5 clean. POLISH: every asteroid (splitting fields + the mine belts) is now a smooth LUMPY rock (subdivided sphere + layered noise + craters, smooth normals, 3 shapes) with a painted stone surface (speckle + crater rings); ORE has glowing red surface CRACKS (was a wireframe cage). space-split makeTools / rockLook. COIN SOUND: coin pickups play their own bright two-note chime (B6 → E7 + shimmer, higher for big coins, climbing in pitch for quick pickups in a row), window.__spaceCoin.
### s461 ASTEROID FIELDS EASY TO FIND (Ben: "I don't see them"): + a NEAR field beside every world (0.3 CELL out, on the side away from the galaxy centre, offset; 13 more, 45 fields total; from Meru the nearest is ~140 u), and every field shows on the minimap (dashed tan ring + its big rocks within 450 u). Cause: the nearest field was ~240 u from Meru, off the usual flight paths.
### s460 SPLITTING ASTEROIDS (Ben: "asteroids that can be split, various types: some into 4, some 2, some 3; the final break leaves a coin"): NEW worlds/space-split.js. 32 fields on the half-cell grid between the worlds (skipping anywhere within 0.42 CELL of a world), 5 big asteroids each, drifting + tumbling. Types by colour: ROCK brown → splits in 2 · ICE pale blue → 3 · ORE dark violet with pulsing red veins → 4. Shoot a big one (hp 22 / 26 / 32): it cracks into its pieces, which fly apart; shoot a piece: dust + a COIN (rock 1 · ice 2 · ore 3 G, via space-combat dropCoin, picked up like pirate coins). A missile shatters a big one outright (one bigger coin). Solid: you bounce (shield absorbs, else hull 8 big / 4 piece), pirates + creatures that ram one are hurt. Pieces fade after 70 s; fields refill (1 big / 20 s) while you are > 450 u away. Phone-light: 2 instanced meshes (180 / 110 on phones), only fields within 450 u simulated. First split shows a how-to toast.
### s459 UNDER ATTACK = STARSHIP RED ALERT (Ben: "an in-space RED ALERT, this is happening NOW"): the square klaxon is replaced by a STARSHIP ALARM: a rising "whoop" siren every half bar (saw + square gliding 330 → 880 Hz through a sweeping resonant filter, a ship-hull echo), computer alert bleeps, a pulsing reactor throb on every beat; drums / bass / stabs / lead as s458. The s457 heroic song is kept as V3 ADVENTURE. Music Workshop → BATTLE MUSIC has V1 / V2 / V3 (space.music.battle.v1 = 1|2|3). Backup backup/space/space-lofi.pre-s458.js.

NEW battle V2 "LET'S GO" (replaces Black Nebula as V2): bright + heroic E major E · B · C#m · A, double-time breakbeat, rolling 16th saw bass with octave jumps, a fast square-pluck arpeggio, brass hits + a soaring saw lead at high danger, risers every 4 bars; builds with the danger. ### s451 SWOOP KEEPS THE SHIP ON SCREEN (Ben: "that made it worse; what makes the station knock the ship off screen?"): the cause was the FOCUS PULL: the swoop slid the camera's look point halfway from the ship toward the focus; installs are small + close (a few u), but a station's focus is big + far (30-50 u away), so the ship was pushed to the edge (worse as the camera turns with your heading). Now the look point never leaves the ship by more than 10 u (4 u at stations); stations focus within 80 u and the swoop only pulls back (33 + 1.6 r, max 95) + up (0.55). Replaces s450b/c.
### s450b/c STATION FRAMING: a station within 110 u always wins the swoop focus (its own dock install used to win and dive in); for big targets the look point sits between ship + station (no forward push), distance = (half the gap + r) × 1.9 (max 150), pitch rises to 0.6 → the whole station + your ship on screen.
### s450 SWOOP AT STATIONS + FAST EXIT (Ben): stations are now swoop FOCUS targets (radius 26 × sc, range 110), so the camera slides to frame them; for big focus targets (r > 12) the swoop keeps its distance (up to 2.7 × r) + a higher angle instead of diving into the station. LEAVING the swoop is twice as fast as entering (swoopK out 1.8 vs in 0.9; camera position + look catch up 2 × faster while it opens out).

NOTE: the Meru dock trade menu is skipped for now (trade at other docks / DSF).
### s416 DOCK WALK, MERU FIRST (Ben: "dock, zoom in, the fox gets out + walks the platform; NO load screens; pause for the animation; an energy shield keeps the air in; the ship on top of the dock, fully visible"): NEW worlds/space-dockwalk.js. DOCK at MERU → GO DOWN now LANDS in the space map itself: the ship flies onto a new BERTH PAD on the dock's south side (fully visible on top) while the camera swoops down close → the fox (the CAST player, built on first landing) steps out → WALK phase: stick / WASD along a new deck on the gantry (glowing edges, lamps) inside a pulsing ENERGY-SHIELD TUBE (+ a shield dome over the pad) → the TELEPORT PAD at the west end ("Teleport to MERU": beam column, the fox fades, then the world's 3D page) or back at the ship ("Board ship": undock). Combat + creatures pause (phase not free). Space Map HUD treats walk like free (prompts + ACTIONS). Debug: __spaceDbg.land('meru'). NEXT: polish (the shield more visible, a hatch on the ship, guards on the deck like the 2D dock), then every other world's dock; Meru Spacedock.dc.html can retire once this matches it.
### s415 SILO HATCH (Ben: "the ore silo hatch opens when the arm drops ore"): the arm's silo now has a hatch on top: a dark collar + accent ring and 2 hinged lids (with glow strips) that swing open (~100°) as the arm arrives over it, an ore glow inside, then close once the chunk has dropped in. Driven by the arm's work cycle (open from late in the swing to just after the drop). space-installs ?v=s415.
### s414 DELUXE MINING ARM (Ben: "the mining arm goes through things, polish the movement, deluxe"): the mine's swinging crane is now a real articulated arm: base ring + turret (yaw), boom + forearm by 2-link IK (elbow-up), 2 hydraulic pistons that extend with the joints, a cable + 3-finger CLAW hanging from a pulley, a blinking tip lamp. A ~14 s eased WORK CYCLE: rest → reach out over the deck edge → dip → lower the claw to the rock → close + a dust puff, an ore chunk in the claw → reel in → lift high → swing (always the way that does NOT pass the hab) over the nearest silo → lower → open: the chunk drops in + the silo flashes → back to rest. The cable sways as a damped pendulum from the swing + reach. Measured over a full cycle: never within clearance of the silo, hab or drill. space-installs ?v=s414.
### s413 LURKERS + RED PEARL BOLTS (Ben: "ships run from the local defences and lurk just outside; pirates attack less inside the 8 worlds, creatures still do; the Machine Fleet rarely, under specific circumstances; every other twin laser = the player's burst but RED, different pitch"): while you are in defended space, pirates / machines RUN to ~30 u outside its edge and LURK there (no shots, no patrol fight; the s410 patrol intercept is off: space-fleets X.intercept to bring it back). Creatures lurk ~34 u outside too. DIRECTOR: inside the 8 worlds' perimeter (1.6 CELL) a crew comes ~half as often (110+ s gaps, 55 % of chances skipped), nothing spawns while you are in defended space; creatures unchanged. MACHINE FLEET: only out past the perimeter (~1 encounter in 7), or within 3 min of you razing a pirate base. ALL OTHER TWIN LASERS (pirates, machines, patrols, pirate-base guns, moth lasers): the Pearl Sail burst (capsule + glow halo + muzzle pop) in RED, sound = the laser at 0.7 pitch (yours stays cyan, full pitch). space-combat / creatures ?v=s413, fleets ?v=s413b.

### s411 THE SOLID BELT (Ben: "spread the asteroids out more round the mine, staggered; running into them hurts the player and any ship / creature chasing; the shield absorbs + bounces you while it is up"; following the 2D Space_world rules): each mine now has 3 STAGGERED lanes of rocks (s411c Ben: room to fly through: radius 18 / 36 / 54, rocks ~18 u apart along each lane, alternate lanes offset half a gap, light jitter, rock radius 1.3-2.8 → surfaces stay ≥ ~9 u apart, the ship is ~7 u wide; ~38 solid rocks per mine) ON the flight plane + a few small ones below for depth. They ORBIT the rig slowly (2D), inner lanes a little faster. SHIELD UP: the shield absorbs the hit (8), you are pushed off AND the rock is shoved 3 u away (2D: "you are pushed apart instead of grinding through it"). SHIELD DOWN: hull -8, a knock-back, 0.75 s grace. Pirates, machines + creatures (not the Belt Serpent, it lives there) that hit a rock take 12 and bounce, so weaving the belt shakes them off. First hit: a hint toast. Lasers still break rocks (back in 25 s). ~70 rocks per mine, 1 instanced draw, far rocks frozen. space-map ?v=s411b, space-combat hit(p, n).
### s410 DEFENDED SPACE + ALWAYS SWOOP (Ben: "swoop should always happen; hostiles shy away at those areas because the planets' patrols defend them"): every world's swoop area (docks, shipyard, fuel, mine, stargate, its station; not pirate bases / nests / machine yard / finds) is a HAVEN (swoop range + 6 u; a world at WAR with you does not protect you). Pirates, the Machine Fleet + creatures never enter a haven (pushed out at its edge); while you are inside one they HOLD at the edge, can't charge / lunge, and their shots FIZZLE on it (cyan splash). space-fleets: every 0.4 s up to 2 free PATROL ships per held hostile INTERCEPT it ("<WORLD> PATROL ENGAGING. You are in defended space."): they orbit it at 18 u and fire bolts in their world colour (ally bolts hit pirates, machines (→ disabled, you can still UNHACK) + creatures); held pirates fire back at them (no damage). Friendly patrols are never foes (no lock-on, missiles, minimap red, fight camera). Camera: the swoop now ALWAYS happens near a model, fight or not. Belt serpents keep their own mine. space-combat ?v=s410b, space-creatures + space-fleets ?v=s410.

Wave frame: a = down the line (world x = -a), d = in front of the crest (world z = zc - d). All tuning in TUNE at the top of surf-break.js.
   RIDE: lineup = lie on the board, stick paddles around, wave comes → PADDLE · TAP 3 (meter; need 3.1) → pop-up + DROP (LATE DROP if steep). Stick = where to point on the face (right = down the line, up = toward the lip, left = back to the curl); no stick = trims to mid-face. Gravity down the face + wave push vs drag, flat shoulder is heavy so the curl catches up. 1 CARVE = BOTTOM TURN (low) / SNAP or OFF THE LIP (high, climbing) / CUTBACK (stick back, ROUNDHOUSE if it ends in the pocket) / CARVE. 2 TRICK = air: 360 · up RODEO FLIP · down SUPERMAN · sideways GRAB (land before it ends or eat it); on the face HANG TEN. 3 JUMP = big air off the lip when climbing (hitting the lip fast also pops a small air). TUBE = low on the face under the lip near the curl (TUBE x.x S on exit). Points × pocket multiplier (closer to the curl) × speed, repeats are worth less.
   WIPEOUTS: OVER THE FALLS (top of the face at the curl), CAUGHT BY THE WHITEWATER / CLOSED OUT IN THE TUBE, ATE IT ON THE LANDING, PEARLED. Fox flies off, board cartwheels on its leash, washing machine under the foam, pops up gasping; crowd OOOH. CAUGHT INSIDE (sat on the wrong side of the peak) = tumble, not counted. Ride ends: KICK OUT (over the back), RODE IT TO THE SAND, OUTRAN THE WAVE, FLEW OUT THE BACK.
   SCORING: wave score = 10·(1 − e^(−points/1500)), ×0.72 after a wipeout, +0.3 for riding it out; five judges' cards ±0.45, high + low struck, middle three averaged. FREE SURF: 3 waves, best two ≥ 11.00 → FINAL vs JOB: Job first, alternating, 3 waves each; Job rides a choreographed line on the same wave (drop, tube, air 360, off the lip, cutback, rodeo flip, kick out; TAP TO SKIP) and scores from TUNE.JOB (7.4 · 6.7 · 8.3, shuffled ±0.3). Best two wins. Win = save flag surfWon + best (jidda.surf.best.v1). Crowd noise + cheers scale with every move.

    1 = neutral: bottom turn / snap by where you are · ↓ BOTTOM TURN (drops low first) · ↑ FLOATER near the curl (rides the falling lip, immune to over-the-falls) else SNAP / OFF THE LIP · ← CUTBACK · → TUBE STALL (hand drag, slows so the curl catches you).
    2 = in the air: 360 · ↑ RODEO FLIP · ↓ SUPERMAN · ← AIR REVERSE · → KICKFLIP (board flips under him) · on the face: HANG TEN · ↓ CHEATER FIVE · ←/→ BARREL ROLL (pops a small air with a roll).

Right: buttons 1 (57 px, bottom edge flush with 2's bottom), 2 (69 px, bottom-right corner), 3 (57 px, above 2, right edge flush with 2's right); small extra (scope/menu) 42 px between them. Tapping the QUEST tip in the top bar opens JOURNAL → QUESTS (tap again closes). CONTROLS v3 (Ben): ITEM BAG tap = open ITEMS, hold 1 s = use the PINNED item (no dot/badge); middle button tap = WEAPONS (scope flashing: tap = SCOPE, hold 1 s = WEAPONS); top-bar ☰ = JOURNAL, with a row at the very top (above the tabs): BACK TO ORBIT (black, gold space-shuttle icon that every 4.5 s rumbles, lights a little flame, lifts off and fades, then settles back) · OPTIONS (sound, phone controls, camera set, reset camera, slow motion) · HOW TO (was INSTRUCTIONS; phone + keyboard controls) · LOAD · SAVE; menu tab text all white, SCOPE tab far LEFT (SCOPE · ITEMS · WEAPONS · JOURNAL · MAP); every close is a white ✕ in a red square; the SCOPE tab has its own row above the tabs: SCOPE · TIME STOPPED + red ✕ on the right; top bar order HP/EN · CR · WEAPONS (scope icon) · MAP · CAMERA · ☰; PAD WORD LOOP (70 s): each control shows its word for 10 s in turn, then its icon again: 1 MELEE → 2 RANGED → 3 JUMP → middle MENU → eye VIEW → bag ITEM, then 10 s of icons only. ONE 40 s word clock so only one button ever shows words: MENU word 10-20 s, MAP word 30-40 s, CAMERA/ANGLE words 3-6.2 s and 23-26.2 s (1.6 s each), icons the rest; camera icon has no box, shows 8 s then CAMERA 1.6 s, ANGLE 1.6 s. JOURNAL (new menu tab between WEAPONS and MAP): CHARACTER = three fox cards BEN / HOPE / NOBLE (selected one filled in its colour; each shows LV, HP bar, XP bar; tap = switch fox; Ben's XP from the shared save, Hope/Noble from save.stats.xpParty / hpParty, level n at 50·n·(n+1) XP), ATTRIBUTES per fox (Ben's design, save.stats.attrParty overrides): BEN STR 7 · SPD 5 · SMT 6 · AIM 5 · HRT 8; HOPE STR 4 · SPD 3 · SMT 8 · AIM 3 · HRT 7 (blind); NOBLE STR 5 · SPD 8 (chair tech + arms) · SMT 6 · AIM 8 (upper-body focus) · HRT 7; selected fox's NAME + LV repeat above ATTRIBUTES; fox cards show LV with a small XP bar beside it (no HP); REPUTATION · MERU (save.stats.repMeru, NEWCOMER/KNOWN/TRUSTED/HERO OF MERU), KARMA meter OUTLAW ↔ HERO per fox (Ben from save.stats.karma, Hope + Noble start at +10; save.stats.karmaParty). RULE (Ben): HP and EN shown in the menu header (Journal, Weapons, every tab) and the top bar are ALWAYS the selected fox's; each fox keeps its own HP/EN pool (move-lab POOL, swapped on switch). Fox cards have no hover effect. Fox switch: the shown fox snaps onto the player spot + leaves POV. In the worlds the quest compass should follow the tracked course. ITEM BAG (bottom-left, stacked just above the EYE, 44 px; moved up so it never touches button 1 at 390 px): tap = use the HOT ITEM (default HEALTH bar; coloured dot + count badge), hold 0.45 s = open the menu on ITEMS (pauses) with a HOT ITEM picker (HEALTH · PEP · CELL, saved in meru.hotItem.v1). Camera button = video camera in a yellow box, cycles icon → CAMERA → ANGLE every 1.6 s. Time label swaps JANUARY 1 (30 s) ↔ SPEED TIME (10 s) loop, on the shared 40 s clock (tap = +1 hour). CAMERA BUTTON (top bar, between CR and WEAPONS): pauses the game, swaps the joystick + buttons for a SET & LOCK CAMERA sheet (viewfinder brackets, rule-of-thirds grid, PAUSED · CAMERA chip; drag the view to angle it, pinch / wheel to zoom; ZOOM − + and TILT ▼ ▲ bars; presets CLOSE · CLASSIC · WIDE · HIGH; ✕ cancels back; LOCK CAMERA saves distance + tilt to meru.combatTune.v1). TIME BLOCK (clock on top, date line under it, left edges aligned): shows the date (JAN 1, 28-day months), every 3 s swaps to PRESS · SPEED UP; each tap skips ahead exactly ONE HOUR (no auto speed; label shows +1 HOUR / +n HOURS for a moment, block tints, rolls the date at midnight); 12-hour clock with AM/PM beside it; game clock starts 10:00 AM (phone portrait: time block right-aligned so the M of AM lines up with the ☰ glyph above), 1 game minute per second, stops while paused. MERU TOP BAR in the Combat Workshop (Ben: show the player experience): same black bar + yellow rule as the Town Square — HP/EN bars, QUEST · MERU TRAINING GROUNDS 'Train with the dummies', period · weather + clock, CR (shared save gold), WEAPONS (opens the menu's weapons tab), ☰ (opens the menu); portrait = two rows like Meru. SCOPE OVERLAY on the view: vignette + scanlines + a sweeping line, CALLED SHOT card (target, range bar with sweet-spot tick, distance + IN RANGE / SWEET SPOT), yellow corner brackets around the target, spinning dashed ring + red crosshair, HEAD / ARM / BODY / LEGS call-outs on leader lines at the right heights with live hit % and queued ×n (tap = queue that shot). SCOPE IN THE MENU (Combat Workshop): the small scope/menu button (38 px) between 1 and 3 swaps its icon scope ↔ menu every 3 s while it pulses; tapping it in scope mode freezes time AND opens the MENU on a new first tab SCOPE (tabs SCOPE · ITEMS · WEAPONS · MAP): the menu becomes a bottom sheet with the called-shots HUD (target, ◀ ▶, BODY/LEGS/ARM/HEAD, queue, CLEAR/EXECUTE) and the camera closes in on the target in the clear view above it; other tabs still work; closing the menu leaves the scope; EXECUTE closes it and fires. ## Rules for every world (see CLAUDE.md)
One connected outdoor map with zones (paths become zones, bracket names kept) + fade interiors + separate battle maps. Off-path wilds with creatures that stay off the path; paths always lined with lamps or trees. Shared save, story/choices, enemy library. Backup before each world. Phone budget.
