## Step 1b — BATTLE POLISH (decided 2 Oct, user) — NOT STARTED
Feel: LIGHT AND ARCADEY (quick, forgiving). Work in the Combat Workshop first (move-lab.js: dummies + new enemy types), then roll into the Arena, Caves and Bridge. Scope, in this order:
1. COMBOS + NEW MOVES (one button stays one button):
   - 1 MELEE tapped in rhythm = a 3-hit chain: slash → back-slash → spin finisher (bigger arc + knockback). Each hit opens a short window (~0.35 s) for the next; miss it and the chain resets. Forgiving: buffered input (a press slightly early still counts).
   - HOLD 1 = HEAVY: charge glow (0.4 s), release = overhead smash, breaks guard, small shockwave.
   - 1 IN THE AIR (after 3 JUMP) = air attack: downward plunge, bounce off the enemy.
   - PARRY = tap DODGE just as a hit lands (~0.15 s window): slow-mo flash, the attacker staggers, the next hit is a critical.
   - MIX: 2 RANGE right after a melee chain = 'launcher shot' finisher (laser burst, EN cost).
   - Combo counter + style letter on screen (the Arena's style rank, made shared).
2. HIT FEEL: hit-stop (40-70 ms freeze on contact, longer on finishers), impact flash on the foe, sparks, knockback scaled by move, camera shake (small), layered hit sounds (light / heavy / crit / parry).
3. EN SYSTEM: the laser costs EN per shot, heavy/launcher cost more; EN refills over time and faster on melee hits (rewards mixing). Top bar EN becomes real.
4. ENEMY LIBRARY (engine/enemies.js): melee (circle, telegraph, swing), ranged (keeps distance, aimed shots with a visible charge), charger (wind-up glow, dash, wall-stun), boss pattern sets (phases like Nelly). Telegraphs are big and readable (arcadey).
5. ONE SHARED ENGINE: merge meru-arena.js and engine/combat.js into engine/battle.js used by the Arena, Caves, Bridge, Nelly's boat fight hooks and every later world.
7. THE SCOPE (2D toggleScope, surface_meru.html ~7394-7720): tap the SCOPE icon (top bar WEAPONS row) = the WORLD FREEZES (slow = 0) and a CALLED SHOTS panel opens. Targets = hostiles (and the pulsing attack target) within weapon range ×1.6, nearest first; ◀ ▶ cycles. Pick a zone per shot: BODY (odds 1.00, dmg ×1.0, reliable), LEGS (0.85, ×0.8, halves its speed), ARM (0.70, ×1.2, disarms), HEAD (0.50, ×2.6, critical + reels). Hit chance = base (0.75 + 0.20 in the range sweet spot at 45% of weapon range + smarts/speed skill, max 0.98, 0 if out of range) × zone odds (head capped 0.88). Queue up to THREE shots (EN cost per shot), CLEAR or EXECUTE: the scope closes and a cinematic volley plays at 1/5 speed (camera holds, each round fired in turn, misses go visibly wide, hits spark + damage + the zone effect), then time snaps back. Floating note: 'Queue up to three called shots, then EXECUTE.' Bring into 3D as part of the battle polish (a VATS-style pause), using the top bar's scope button. BUILT IN THE COMBAT WORKSHOP (move-lab.js, 2 Oct): Q / SCOPE button freezes time, yellow reticle on the target (nearest first, ◀ ▶ / arrows cycle), zone buttons 1-4 with live hit %, queue of 3 (EN each), CLEAR / EXECUTE (Enter): volley at 1/5 speed with zone-coloured bolts, misses fly wide, hits pop damage + SLOWED / DISARMED / CRITICAL. Range 22 m, sweet spot 9.9 m. Scope camera: closes in on the target from the player's side, sized so the whole body fits the clear band between the top and the CALLED SHOTS panel (camera.setViewOffset shifts the frame up; distance from the band height + FOV); key hints and bottom buttons hide while scoping; the volley keeps the framing. Still to do: put it in the real fights.
6. HEALTH / DEATH / RESPAWN: shared rules (hurt flash + i-frames, low-HP warning, knocked out → respawn at the last safe spot with a small CR cost or none, heal items from the wheel).

- ENEMY LIBRARY brain: engine/creature-ai.js createBrain(g, ck) → { role (boss / charge / ranged / melee from userData), hp, max, range, speed, update(dt, dist, state, st) → next state, moveSign(d), hurt(n, weak, state) → state, strike }. Rules: approach to range (ranged keeps 2.6–5.5 m), cooldown, windup → attack → recover (chargers → stagger); every 3rd hit staggers (bosses 6th); armor break at 50% (bosses + 25%); weak point ×1.6, ×3 while recovering/staggered; committed attacks only interrupted by a weak-point hit; Husk / Attendants / Siphon never flinch. Workshop: TRY THE AI toggle (creature fights the circling fox; HIT / HIT WEAK POINT; readout role, HP, fox HP; respawns 3 s after death). Menus pause the game (St.paused). CAMERA sheet: setCam/lookBy/zoomBy, LOCK saves meru.townCam.v1. Key 4 now opens ITEMS (the radial wheel is retired). Kept as before: dialogue, prompt, darts, lock pick, jukebox, sermon, fight panel, minigame panel, intro.

## ✓ KYOTO SUMO HALL [kyotoSumoHall] · SUMO STREAK — SPEC (Ben's answers; v1 BUILT, see below)

- PLAY: real-time brawl. Joystick circles/moves in the ring. 1 PUSH (tsuki shove) · 2 SLAP (harite flurry) · 3 GRAB (belt hold; while held, push = yorikiri carry, 4 = throw) · 4 THROW (nage, needs a grab). Balance/stamina meter per wrestler.
- WIN BY: push out of the ring · throw so he touches the ground · slap-flurry ring-out · lift + carry out (yorikiri). Each move gets a kimarite name popup (OSHIDASHI, UWATENAGE, TSUKIDASHI, YORIKIRI).
- STRUCTURE: one endless bout streak (score attack). Opponents get bigger + tougher each win; one loss ends the streak. Opponents: generic rikishi from human-kit in different mawashi colours, growing in height/build/AI per win.
- DIFFICULTY: easy fun (wide ring edge forgiveness, slow AI early, generous throws).
- REWARD: at 5 wins in one streak → relic `kyotoSumoTrophy` + flag `mawashiSky` (unlocks a SKY BLUE #7dd3fc mawashi for Ben Sumo). Gold per win, best streak stat `kyoto.sumo.streak.best`.
- CEREMONY (all): ring-entry walk under the hanging roof (tsuriyane) · salt throw before each bout · shiko stomp (tap to stomp, crowd cheers) · gyoji referee with a gunbai fan calling HAKKEYOI! to start and NOKOTTA during the bout · crowd throws zabuton cushions on an upset (beating a much bigger opponent).
- HALL: grand tournament hall interior. Raised clay dohyo with straw-bale ring, hanging shrine roof with 4 coloured tassels, tiered crowd on 4 sides (instanced, phone budget), big vertical nobori banners, ring-side judges, lantern light.
- MOBILE FIRST: test 390x844 + 844x390; camera frames both wrestlers side-on; buttons via Game HUD (VEH_SHORT sumo: PUSH · SLAP · GRAB · THROW).

## ✓ KYOTO SWORD DUEL v1 [kyotoBarracks yard] vs THE SECOND (2D `kendo` rebuilt side-on 2.5D, Street Fighter style)
- FILES: `Kyoto Sword Duel.dc.html` + `minigames/kyoto/sword-duel.js` (createDuel) + `minigames/kyoto/kendo-2d.json` (GAYA.kendo verbatim) + `Kyoto Sword Duel Phone Preview.dc.html`. Game HUD vehicle "duel" (1 HIGH · 2 MID · 3 LOW + icons). Backup: backup/kyoto/Game HUD pre-duel.dc.html.
- Ben's answers: side-on 2.5D, Ben · Sumo in plain dark gi + hakama vs THE SECOND, real katana (toon sparks, no blood), stick + 3 buttons, hold BACK = guard (no 4th button), easy fun, power meter, parry, best of 3, slow-mo final hit, cherry-blossom yard at sunset, + combos and supers.
- PLAY: stick ←→ walk (fwd/back speeds from 2D) · hold BACK = guard (standing guards HIGH + MID, crouch-back guards MID + LOW) · DOWN = crouch. HIGH (men, overhead) / MID (tsuki thrust) / LOW (leg sweep). Hits chain from a landed hit's early recovery = COMBO (counter, 0.88 scaling); HIGH→MID→LOW = SANDAN-GIRI (×1.6 + knockback). Guard just before the hit (within 0.15 s of pressing back) = PARRY (attacker stunned, slow-mo blink, power +30). Chip damage on guard = 2D chip 0.18.
- SUPERS: MASH any attack (4 presses in 0.8 s) = HYAKURETSU HARITE (E. Honda hundred-hand slaps, 10 hits). DOWN → FORWARD + attack = SHIO (a handful of salt flies, DAZES him 1.6 s with stars). Power meter (dealt +18, taken +25, parry +30): full → two attacks at once (or Q / 4) = ISSEN power strike (lunge, breaks guard, 40 dmg). KO = slow-mo + white flash + camera push-in (longer on the deciding round).
- Rounds: best of 3, 75 s (2D seconds), time-out = higher HP %. HP: Ben 160 / Second 120 (2D youHp/hp). AI easy: telegraphed wind-ups, guards sometimes, rare parries; round 2/3 a bit sharper; uses ISSEN when full. Tweak difficulty Normal. Win = 80 g + 200 XP, flag kyotoDuelWon, stat kyoto.duel.wins.
- YARD: barracks facade (plaster + timber, tiled roof, lit windows), bokken rack, nobori (八 門 武), lanterns, 4 sakura trees + falling petals, low sunset sun + long shadows, 2 kneeling samurai watching. SOUND: battle taiko pattern + koto (theatre-audio MOODS.battle), kiai shouts, sword swish, metal clang + ring on parry, slash thuds, slaps, salt hiss, crowd gasp + applause on KO.
- NOT YET: link from Kyoto barracks; the Second's 2D dialogue / reward lines; blade-lock (2D) left out (Ben didn't pick it).
- DUEL v2 POLISH: hit-stop on every hit (longer on ISSEN), victim flashes white, white slash arcs (gold on ISSEN), HP damage-lag bars (red/amber trail drains after 0.5 s), big HITS combo counter on the attacker's side, red glint on the Second's blade during his wind-up (gold on any ISSEN) so attacks are readable, footstep dust + step sounds, dust burst on ISSEN, fighters walk in to their marks each round, ROUND / HAJIME / K.O. slam-in scale, camera pushes in during combos. Backup: backup/kyoto/sword-duel pre-polish.js.

## PEARL SAIL TOWER [pearlSailTower] — side-on battle climb (Ben, s35o)
Files: `Pearl Sail Tower.dc.html` (Game HUD + floor card + boss bar + banner + Welcome Card + cleared card; ?embed=1 posts 8gates:minigame-back; ?autostart=1 skips the card) + `worlds/pearl-sail.js` (createPearlSail, Game HUD engine contract; debug window.__pearl._dbg.tp(x, y)).
Ben's picks: Pearl Sail · side-on 2.5D (Metroid) · 6 floors + roof boss · enemies: swooping DRONES, patrolling CRAWLERS, wall TURRETS, ceiling DROPPERS, SHIELDED GUARDS (front blocks, hit from behind) · double jump from the start (the Combat Workshop's: tap 3 in the air, flip) · boss SUDS-9 the rogue window-cleaning robot on its gondola, then the relic · walk in the tower's front door in Meru 2 · player only · the tower's own look (glass offices, overrun by its own security bots).
Combat = Combat Workshop tuning (move-lab.js loadTune: walk, jump 8, gravity 24, swing/windup/reach/combo window/finisher, sword 25, laser 15, fire rate, energy) + its rules: 1 slash chain, on the beat = PERFECT x1.3, 3rd = finisher; 2 laser (stick up / W = aim up, light auto-aim); 3 jump, again in the air = double jump. Down + jump drops through ledges. Coyote time + jump buffer.
Floors (FLOORS in pearl-sail.js; one-way ledges, the slab hole alternates sides, a yellow grate fills it; route check warns in the console if a step > 2.5 m up or > 4.5 m across): 1 LOBBY (revolving door = exit, E) · 2 OPEN OFFICE · 3 SERVER ROOM (solid racks) · 4 EXECUTIVE SUITE · 5 ATRIUM (pendant lights) · 6 MAINTENANCE · ROOF. Checkpoint = first landing on each new floor; KO = respawn there with full HP. Bots drop pearls (+12 HP). Items heal from the bag.
SUDS-9 (900 HP): SPRAY (lobbed soap bubbles, shootable) · SWEEP (gondola docks, red strip = JUMP over the squeegee; phase 3 adds a yellow HIGH sweep = STAY DOWN) · then DOCKED 2.3 s = WEAK POINT (full damage; otherwise the dome takes 40 % shots / 60 % sword) · phase 2+ releases drones. You can stand on the gondola deck. Win: relic 'pearlSail', flag pearlSailCleared, +150 CR first time (+25 after), best time stat pearlSailBest.
Meru 2 entry: L.BUILDINGS 'pearlSail' (open, hiring.play → no NOW HIRING board; the prompt says BATTLE · PEARL SAIL) at the landmark's revolving door (383, 222.6).
s35p (Ben: could not reach floor 2, no hint): every ledge step is now 1.6 m (was up to 2.4, needed a perfect apex double jump), route check warns above 2.0; a pulsing yellow ARROW floats over the next ledge up (then the ceiling grate); lobby has no turret; hurt knockback 4 (was 7). s35q FIX (verifier): the top ledges sat under the solid slab (1 m head room → shoved into the hole column, fell). Now per floor: 1.6 → 3.2 → 4.8 (that one reaches into the hole column) → 6.4 INSIDE the hole column → grate 8; the X push ignores head overlaps < 0.3 m; route check warns on head room. DEMO: Welcome Card WATCH THE DEMO = autopilot (climbs with the same jump / double jump, slashes + shoots bots, jumps the boss sweeps, hits SUDS-9 when docked, takes the relic; no damage; 6 s with no new height = hops to the next ledge); yellow DEMO PLAYING chip = take over. s35r ENEMIES + GRAPHICS (backup backup/pearl-sail/pearl-sail.pre-polish.js): every bot has a glowing eye, flashes white when hit, gets knocked back, shows a small HP bar for 2.5 s, and dies with a hit-stop, a spin / flip arc, chunks that bounce, then a glow pop. CRAWLERS crouch (eye flickers, '!') then LUNGE 3 m. DRONES + TURRETS show a red aiming laser while they wind up (dodge it). GUARDS: shield flashes on a block; after a bash they STAGGER 1 s with the shield down ('OPEN!' = hit the front). Graphics: real 3D city outside the glass in 3 depth rows (parallax as you climb), fog, light shafts per floor, floor-tinted light (server room blue, executive warm), slash arc (gold on the finisher), laser glow + muzzle flash, double-jump ring, vignette. - REEL: young tan fox, olive fishing vest with 6 lures on the chest, red cap with a yellow badge; fast, record-obsessed lines (Claude's). Moves to each station during the job.
- GAME 1 · THE BAIT JOB (yellow ring in the middle, E): a regular (the Fisherman, Kia, Otto, Marla, Pell, Michael Jay, Flick) orders worms + a lure + minnows and brings a catch. 1 DIG: worms pop out of the 8 holes for 2 s, tap them (4-6). 2 TIE: tap the lure on the card (RED SPINNER / YELLOW POPPER / BLUE MINNOW; wrong = Reel names it), it goes in the vise; drag along the dots: THREAD through the eye · WRAP (8 zigzag dots) · TUCK + PULL; the white line follows your finger; off the dots = "TANGLE" (less bonus); the knot pulls tight. 3 SCOOP: drag the net through the tank, silver minnows only (red = shop pets, Reel: "NOT GUS!"); in portrait the fish keep to the middle 1.8 m of the tank. 4 WEIGH: their fish hangs on the scale, the needle swings (slowly settling), tap in the green band; if it beats the board record their name goes on the RECORD BOARD (camera shows the board). 5 SORT & ICE: 6 fish on the tray (3 big, 3 small), drag (or tap, then tap the chest) into BIG / SMALL. Customer pays. GENTLE: no fail. ~100 gold a job.
- GAME 2 · DOCK FISHING (free, stay as long as you like; E on the FISH ring at the jetty end, or anywhere on the lake shore / any jetty once you own a Bamboo rod): tap the water to cast (3 white RIPPLES = fish, casting near one = faster + rarer bites); little bobs are nibbles, the big dip + yellow "!" = TAP; HOLD to reel, let go when it pulls (tension meter; at full the line goes slack a moment, never snaps); the fish leaps to you and the card shows name, kg, gold + tags NEW / BIGGEST / RARE / NEW MERU RECORD (goes on the board as YOU). Species = the 2D game's six (Sunny Bluegill, Copper Carp, Silver Minnow, Rainbow Trout, Golden Koi, Ancient Catfish), weights from length. Card (left, same spot as the shops) has two 44 px buttons: BAIT (Plain Worm / Shiny Lure / Golden Bait you own) and FISH BOOK (caught ×, best kg, Nelly, the Meru records). Rod in your hand (sword hidden while fishing), camera high behind you so the water fills the screen.
- NELLY (rare: 1.2 %, 6 % with Golden Bait): huge shadow, long reel; she rises out of the lake, roars, the line goes slack, and she flips you a HULL PEARL (item hullPearl). Book: NELLY · MET ×n.
- RODS: Twig (start, range 12 m) · Bamboo (15 m, faster reel, fish ANY shore/jetty) · Steel (18 m, fastest, least strain). BAITS: Plain Worm (free) · Shiny Lure (bigger fish) · Golden Bait (rare fish + Nelly); used up per catch. Lucky Hook = +10 % rare.
- TACKLE COUNTER (by the front door): Shiny Lure ×3 15 G · Golden Bait 40 G · Bamboo Rod 60 G · Steel Rod 150 G (next tier only).

A clean job (4+ clean steps) adds Shiny Lure ×2. - ONE SESSION, 8 STEPS (yellow ring by the desk, E): 1 GEAR UP: tap HARNESS / SHOES / CHALK BAG in the card's order (wrong = Big Tall names it), drag the FIGURE 8 knot dots. 2 ROUTE SETTING: drag (or tap-tap) your 5 holds (session colour) onto the white chalk rings in the cave. 3 BOULDER: tap the next hold of YOUR colour; decoys of other colours = slip back one; 2 wrong in a row (or at the start) = fall on the mat, start again. 4 DYNO: hold to charge (gold band 65-92 %), let go, tap as your hands pass the lip hold (slow-mo flight); too weak / missed = fall, Big Tall puts you back. 5 TOP ROPE: GRIP METER: hold = the reach bar runs, let go in the gold band (narrower on the roof) to reach the next hold; too short = lose grip; overreach = fall; grip drains (faster on the roof), CHALK UP button ×3 (+35 %); falls drop you 2 holds on Big Tall's rope. Ring the bell (time goes on the TOP ROPE board). 6 RAPPEL: tap = push off and drop, tap = brake on each of 3 yellow tapes; too late = Big Tall brakes for you. 7 BELAY: a Meru regular climbs the green route; HOLD to take in slack (bar, rope sags), at 2 random holds they FALL: tap within 1.3 s (tight catch < 1 m slack = bonus; missed = Big Tall grabs it), then HOLD to lower them. 8 SPEED WALL: 3-2-1, tap the next hold as fast as you can (miss-tap = slip), tap the finish button; Tiny climbs ~0.74 s a hold; lose = rematch (Tiny slower each time, 3 tries, then you move on). ~150 gold a session.
- PRIZES per session in turn: CLIMBING SHOES (red, worn) → HARNESS + ROPE (red belt + leg loops, orange rope coil, chalk bag) → GRAPPLING HOOK (item grapplingHook) → SUMMIT MEDAL (item summitMedal + the frame by the door) → then +20 gold. 6+ clean steps = +15 gold. While climbing you always wear harness + shoes (grey rental shoes before you own yours); the sword / gun are hidden. MY GEAR hook (west wall, once you own any) toggles shoes / harness for the rest of Meru 2 (save stat rkWear; shoes hide Lace's shoe overlay while on). - JOBS, inside (all 12): polish the throne + crown · roll out the red carpet for a visitor · announce guests at the door (match name to crest) · light the chandeliers (lower, light, raise) · shelve the library books by colour / number · find a lost book with the ladder · count the treasury gold (stacks of 10) · guard the vault (spot the thief) · set the council table (12 places) · move the pins on the 8-gates war map · serve the King's dinner · royal portrait (hold still while he paints).

RUINS MUSEUM + PERMIT OFFICE DELUXE — BEN'S ANSWERS (s123, do not re-ask): SCOPE: Ruins Museum [meruRuinsInterior museum] + Permit Office [meruPermitOffice]; the Ruins Cave gets a LOOK PASS at the end. MUSEUM KEEPERS: OLD SAGE + a young DIGGER apprentice (dig-site jobs; Claude named her SANDY). SIZE: DOUBLE IT (hall + back room). MUSEUM JOBS (all 10): brush the dirt off a find · glue a broken pot back · sort relics by age · appraise: real or fake? · restore a floor mosaic · polish the display cases · catalogue new finds (tag + shelf) · dig a square in the pit (trowel + sieve) · night watch: catch the relic thief · rub a stone carving onto paper. RELIC OFFER (2D standing offer stays) + a COLLECTION WALL that fills as you sell + YOUR NAME on each relic you brought in + a daily WANTED relic that pays double. PERMIT OFFICE (Spade) JOBS (all 8): stamp the permits (right stamp) · file papers in the pigeonholes · survey a plot (stakes + string) · measure with the theodolite · deliver a permit to a dig team · find the lost map in the office · sort the mail · spot the forged permit. BIG PERMIT REWARD: a DIG PERMIT = you can dig for relics in the desert. CAVE: look pass (torches, drips, bats, crystals) · after the story the bandits leave and it becomes a DIG SITE · a HIDDEN CHAMBER with the 9th Key lore. PRIZES: explorer hat (worn) · explorer outfit (Tailor) · trowel + brush on your belt · name on the museum DONORS plaque · your own relic case in the museum · golden trowel trophy + gold · free permit renewals. LOOK + LIFE (all 8): sun shafts + dust motes · torches flicker, dark corners at night · visitors by time of day · diggers coming and going with finds · sand blowing in the door · old stone hum / wind in the ruins · bats at dusk outside the cave · a dig team working in the desert.
FOUND (s123): in Meru 2 the Ruins Museum + Permit Office were EMPTY city shells (generic stone / wood floor), the Sage + Spade stood OUTSIDE their doors as path speakers, and Meru 2 had no relic selling yet.

## COVER AI · BUILT (s131, "cover AI for the bandits"; backups backup/salt-battle/*pre-cover*)
Ben's picks: throwers + brawlers + lookouts take cover (shield bandits + chargers stay out) · pop out 2.5 s · cover props break after a few hits, then he is exposed · ALL extras: card table flip, wounded retreat, flankers, blind throws, taunt barks, red ! before he pops · the PLAYER auto-crouches by low cover.
- FILES: engine/cover-ai.js = coverAI(ctx, { role(e), pose, lines, flip: [prop kinds], whistle, pop }) → { floor(A), upd(e, dt, A, walkTo, see, dist) (true = handled · false = the engine brain runs, used for the brawler RUSH + 'open' fallback), shield(e, d, fx, fz), playerCrouch(A, dt), tick(dt), bark(e, key) }. SHARED: Pepper uses the same file with its own lines.
- SPOTS: built from the floor's solids on every floor load (X.floorReady): low cover (h 0.75-1.7: crates, counters, cash tables, felt tables) = spots every 1.5 m round the sides, pop = stand up · tall cover (crate rows, walls, tanks) = corner spots only, pop = step past the edge. A spot is good when its solid sits between it and you; scored by distance + a band per role (thrower 6-13 m, lookout 8-15, brawler 3.5-9) + a clear straight run; claimed one bandit per spot.
- BRAIN: patrol → spots you (bark, alerts bandits within 10 m) → run to cover → DUCK 1.2-2.2 s (faces you, crouched) → red ! 0.5 s → POP 2.5 s: THROWER aims (red line) + throws bottles at your chest (at your knees if you are ducked) · BRAWLER shouts then RUSHES (engine punch/lunge) and finds new cover · LOOKOUT peeks + WHISTLES (old lookout code). Flanked (cover no longer between) → new spot (brawler within 7 m rushes instead). Cover broken → EXPOSED! + MY COVER! → new spot. Too close → throwers back off, brawlers rush. Every 3rd brawler is a FLANKER (spots 60-120° round you from the group). Below 40 % HP → I'M HIT! → retreats to far cover for 3.5 s. Throwers BLIND-THROW over the top (40 % per duck: arcing bottle, red ring where it lands, 9 dmg, ducking does not save you). No spot → 'open' 2.2 s on the old brain, then tries again; stuck 1 s → same.
- CARD TABLE FLIP (floor 3 felt tables): a bandit without good cover runs behind a table (≤ 5.5 m), FLIP IT! → the table tips onto its edge toward you (instanced parts rotated, 0.38 s), becomes a 1.3 m low wall + a new cover spot.
- HITS: a ducked bandit hit from the far side of his cover → the hit lands on the cover (COVER; props crack + break: crate 3, cash table 2, felt 3, counter 4) · walls just stop it. Flank him or break it.
- PLAYER CROUCH: standing still by low cover while an alerted bandit (or the boss) is within 18 m → ducks (fox drops 0.5 m, legs bent, COVER chip; first time: DUCKED · SHOOT OR SWING TO POP UP). Shooting / swinging pops you up for 0.8 s. Enemy bolts only hit a ducked fox below 1.05 m.
- BARKS: white speech boxes over the bandit (ink rule, Archivo, flush left, no corners), 1.6 s, one every 0.9 s across the floor, each bandit max every 3.5 s. Salt lines: THERE HE IS! · A FOX! GET HIM! · INTRUDER! · COME OUT, FOX! · SALT RUNS THIS TOWN! · FLANK HIM! · FLIP IT! · MY COVER! · I'M HIT! · HEADS UP! · TOO CLOSE!
- ENGINE (pearl-floor3d.js, all behind X): FA gained S, solid, props, fireBolt, segHitsWall, hitProp, tele, damage, groundAt · damage() asks X.cover first · X.floorReady after buildArt · P.crouch / P.popT / crouch pose · enemy bolt vs ducked fox height. Pearl Sail unchanged without a mode.
- TESTED (preview): floor 1 bandits go rush / duck / tell / pop, bubbles show, player ducks by the small crate; floor 3 a table got flipped (h 1.3), no console errors.
NOT YET: Ben's phone pass 390x844 + 844x390 (bubble size, the duck feel, does the crouch trigger too often), tuning (pop 2.5 s, how many throwers end up 'open' in the card room: few low spots far enough from you), a full play-through by hand.
TRY THIS (cover): Salt Building → floor 1 · walk up the rug and watch them dive behind crates · shoot the crate a bandit hides behind until it breaks · walk round the side of one (flank him) · stop next to a small crate and let a thrower aim at you (you duck, the bottle hits the crate) · floor 3: watch a bandit FLIP a card table.
- s131b DEEP DIVE: SQUAD PACING (max 2 throwers up at once; the rest wait + taunt) · COVER ME! (a brawler going in makes up to 2 nearby throwers pop and throw) · AUTO-AIM prefers an exposed bandit over one tucked behind cover (X.aimCost, +7 m) · the player only ducks when the low block is between him and somebody after him (then stays down, no flicker) · relaxed 2nd spot pass (no straight-run rule, within 9 m) = fewer 'open' throwers · bubbles sit above the red ! · COVER text max every 0.7 s · dt can never go negative (frame0 + damp clamps; the debug advance() could blow the crouch value up).

- HOURS: 8:00-20:00 for every shop; 24 h: Tavern, Casino, Meru Lanes, homes, cluster lobbies, Police, stations, hospital, motel, fire station, barracks, castle. Keepers walk in at 7:00, leave at 20:00 (some via the Tavern / Casino / Lanes for a quick one), and wait for you to leave first.

Routes: A* on a 2 m grid over the colliders (sidewalks / paths / plazas cheap, grass dearer, car lanes 3x), worked out only when someone walks near you (≤ 6 ms a frame on phones), cached both ways.
- FOLLOW IN: walk into a shop after someone and they are inside, looking round 2-6 m from the door (not in the Market: it has its own roster browsers).
- TALK: one line (≤ 20 words) where they're going: open the shop / home to <flat> / popping into X / the Tavern never closes / on the beat.

## s193 FOX SHIELD (Ben: start with a shield, react where it was hit, pulse on hit; modelled on the 2D Space map SCREEN)
- NEW engine/fox-shield.js: a bubble he stands INSIDE (shader: breathing cyan rim + dark casing at the very edge so it reads on light AND dark floors). A hit lights + BULGES the struck section (stays where it landed, spreads, beats like glass springing back), a white bloom at the contact point, 9 sparks skidding ALONG the surface, a number. Space-map rules: bank 100 · 1.2 per damage · refills only after 3 quiet s (full in ~28 s) · empty = SHIELD DOWN (shockwave, 0.6 s safety) · relights at half (SHIELD UP) · below 22% it gutters. Shows when foes are near or it is struck, fades out otherwise.
- Hooks: fox.userData.shield. engine/combat.js hurtPlayer(dmg, from) asks the shield first (Meru 2 + every combat.js map). Pearl 3D / Salt hurt() asks it first (before the SHIELD pickups). Meru 2 re-attaches it after outfit swaps.

- Lab: HIT SHIELD (from the camera side) + BARRAGE · 6 HITS, shows the bank %.

Energy POURS IN to support the spot: bolts stream inward to the contact point, the patch thickens to deep electric blue and PULSES (beat 26/s) for ~0.9 s while a white-hot core throbs at the contact, then it settles. INTENSITY 0..1 layers it in: calm = kick + bass + hats, 0.45+ = full drums + arp, 0.78+ = the lead + open hats + fills. One shared player (window.__battleMusic). Mute-all silences it. Volume saved in localStorage 'battle.music'.

Same API, so every map + the lab pick it up.

## STORY ARC NOTE (Ben, s300) — also in CLAUDE.md
The Machine Fleet has been HACKED; nobody on Meru knows. The player frees the Fleet and gives the robots free agency + a power source, so they can choose to help the foxes or do their own thing. That source sustains today's robots but can't let them grow; to grow they must work with the foxes, sharing resources and space. Robots = hacked victims, not villains.

  14 actions defined: SCAN · STEALTH · STEAL · HACK · CALL HOPE / NOBLE · PHOTO MODE · PLACE MARKER · WAVE · SIT / REST · THROW · CLIMB / GRAB · CALL SHIP · SEARCH · TRACK QUEST.
  PEARL SAIL does 11 of them: SCAN (10 EN, 6 s detective view: screen darkens, robots / gates / pickups / marker glow with labels: HACKED ROBOT, GATE, ENERGY…) · STEALTH toggle (crouch-walk 55 % speed, robots see you from about half as far) · STEAL (behind a robot within 2.6 m: +30 EN, 35 % chance it notices and attacks) · HACK (within 3.2 m, not the boss: stop the bar in the green 3 times, 2 misses = locked out + 8 damage; success = the robot is FREE: stops fighting, blue burst, St.freed++) · PHOTO MODE (HUD + SUPER hidden, paused, tap to return) · PLACE MARKER (blue beam, one at a time, shows in SCAN) · WAVE (arm wave pose + HI!) · SIT / REST (no robot within 14 m: +6 HP/s, moving stands you up) · THROW (stone arcs up to 8 m; robots within 7 m of the landing turn to look for 3 s and stop seeing you) · SEARCH (15 s cooldown: shows pickups within 14 m, 45 % chance to turn up an energy cell) · TRACK QUEST (banner: next gate + distance / the Warden / exit open).
  NOT in Pearl (shown only where they work, later maps): CALL HOPE / NOBLE (needs the team following), CLIMB / GRAB (needs ledges / ropes), CALL SHIP (space docks). STEAL from FOXES (karma drop + guards chase) = later on town maps.

- ORE SHAFT STORY (Ben, s364, do not re-ask):
  - The station was BUILT ON TOP OF AN OLD MINING FACILITY. Down the shaft: a BIIIIG ROOM with GIANT PIECES OF ASTEROID that the bots are harvesting for resources. MACHINES + CONVEYOR BELTS: bots place ORE on belts that go UP; RUBBLE goes on belts to the TRASH CHUTE that goes DOWN.
  - Meru has a second ore processing facility; this one was a helpful second, and the interruption in ore production HAS BEEN NOTICED. There is a PILE-UP OF ORE: the bots were ordered to harvest and DIVERT it, right under the noses of station security.
  - At first only some bots were hacked; slowly ALL of them became hacked. They set up the TRANSMITTER (= the SIGNAL RELAY boss) that sends a signal DOWN TO PLANET MERU, hacking the bots of Meru. Once it is DESTROYED, the bots on Meru return to normal.
  - BUT some bots CHOOSE to help the hacker even when freed: they may still GATE IN at some places on Meru after the signal is gone (not many). Their reasoning = a storyline Ben writes later.
  - The player + R-8 go on a mission to FREE bots and TEACH THEM ABOUT FREEDOM.
  - R-8 = personal assistant to the ENGINEERING department. The Chief keeps fixing him, but he keeps ALMOST being hacked, shorting out, acting strange. The Chief still sends R-8 along on this mission into the battle area.
  - FLOODING: during the last attempt to get in and subdue the hacked bots, a WATER MAIN BURST: flooding in the big asteroid rooms and other areas across the 3 floors.

### s487 CHART PLOTTING (Kufa Station · Maps & Charts · Old Merrit). NEW worlds/dsf-charts.js makeChartTable: a new job on Merrit's own parchment chart table (canvas surface over the table, console kit; the orrery + rod hide while you play). 5 charts in 150 s: KUFA (copper dot, left) → a port (red square, right: GAYA LANE, MERU GATE…). Hazards ROCKS / GRAVITY WELL (rings pull in) / ION STORM (red hatch); the straight line always crosses one. TAP the chart = the line bends through that point (inserted on the nearest leg, max 6 turns), DRAG a turn to move it; red legs = crossing a hazard, red X = where the fuel runs DRY. Pad 1 SAIL (the ship flies the line; hits = LOST) · 2 UNDO · 3 CLEAR. Clean = 4-16 G (tighter line = more; TIGHT LINE stamp > 85 %). Every course is checked solvable (grid search sets the fuel at 1.2× that route). One chart has an UNLOGGED SIGNAL (cyan ping off the lane, extra fuel): sail within reach of it = +8 G, "…NOT OUR ORDERS… HELP US…", flag kuBuoyLogged → Merrit note on leaving (kuBuoySaid). ★ 3 · ★★ 4 · ★★★ 5 clean. Stats kuChartsBest, kuChartsShifts.

### s451 SWOOP KEEPS THE SHIP ON SCREEN (Ben: "that made it worse; what makes the station knock the ship off screen?"): the cause was the FOCUS PULL: the swoop slid the camera's look point halfway from the ship toward the focus; installs are small + close (a few u), but a station's focus is big + far (30-50 u away), so the ship was pushed to the edge (worse as the camera turns with your heading). Now the look point never leaves the ship by more than 10 u (4 u at stations); stations focus within 80 u and the swoop only pulls back (33 + 1.6 r, max 95) + up (0.55). Replaces s450b/c.

### s450 SWOOP AT STATIONS + FAST EXIT (Ben): stations are now swoop FOCUS targets (radius 26 × sc, range 110), so the camera slides to frame them; for big focus targets (r > 12) the swoop keeps its distance (up to 2.7 × r) + a higher angle instead of diving into the station. LEAVING the swoop is twice as fast as entering (swoopK out 1.8 vs in 0.9; camera position + look catch up 2 × faster while it opens out).

### s432 A LOFI SONG FOR EVERY WORLD (Ben: "unique lofi per planet that fades between; keep the current one as the player planet music; Meru more epic as the centre of the galaxy"). engine/space-lofi.js THEMES (all 78 BPM + the same 8-bar grid, so any two crossfade cleanly, equal-power ~5 s; only the songs fading in/out are scheduled): HOME = NEBULA DRIFT (the original, kept for the player's new home world) · OPEN SPACE = VOID DRIFT (A minor, sparse bells + pad, half-time) · MERU = HEART OF THE GALAXY (the epic one: D minor i-VI-III-VII, choir pad, detuned brass horn lead, taiko hits + rolls, a swell into bar 1, lantern bells) · SHASTA = SNOWLIGHT (E major 9ths, bells, soft pad, half-time brush, wind) · LUXOR = SUN DIAL (D phrygian, oud pluck lead, harp arpeggio, tabla toms + shaker, sand) · UR = RED CANYON (A minor, harp lead, half-time, long echo pings) · GAYA = FIRST FLAME (G lydian, flute, harp arpeggio, shuffle, ember crackles) · ZION = SALT FLATS (B♭ mixolydian, marimba, offbeat stabs, bouncy kick, sparkle) · NEBO = TIDE GLIDER (C major 9, whistle, pad, waves) · KUFA = CRYSTAL MARKET (E minor, vibraphone, swung shuffle, chimes) · JIDDA = SURF SUNSET (F major, steel drum, reggae one-drop + stabs, waves). Melodies from a seeded generator over each song's chords (same every visit). Battle "Red Shift" now follows the current song's chords. Space map: nearest centre world within 0.55 CELL picks the song (else open space), toast "NOW PLAYING · <WORLD> · <TITLE>". Backup backup/space/space-lofi.pre-s432.js.

NEW synth thrust in space-map (until the Runway files come): soft pinkish noise in 3 layers: a low RUSH (bandpass 380-1300 Hz) + a deep swell (lowpass 160) that rise with your actual SPEED, a bright JET (highpass) while bursting; silent when still. When the Runway THRUST files arrive (sfx/thrustSmallLoop … thrustMachineLoop, thrustPuff / Start / Stop) they take over automatically: hull picks small / heavy / huge, burst = thrustBurstLoop, nearby pirates / machines play theirs, start / stop puffs. ### s414 DELUXE MINING ARM (Ben: "the mining arm goes through things, polish the movement, deluxe"): the mine's swinging crane is now a real articulated arm: base ring + turret (yaw), boom + forearm by 2-link IK (elbow-up), 2 hydraulic pistons that extend with the joints, a cable + 3-finger CLAW hanging from a pulley, a blinking tip lamp. A ~14 s eased WORK CYCLE: rest → reach out over the deck edge → dip → lower the claw to the rock → close + a dust puff, an ore chunk in the claw → reel in → lift high → swing (always the way that does NOT pass the hab) over the nearest silo → lower → open: the chunk drops in + the silo flashes → back to rest. The cable sways as a damped pendulum from the swing + reach. Measured over a full cycle: never within clearance of the silo, hab or drill. space-installs ?v=s414.

### s410 DEFENDED SPACE + ALWAYS SWOOP (Ben: "swoop should always happen; hostiles shy away at those areas because the planets' patrols defend them"): every world's swoop area (docks, shipyard, fuel, mine, stargate, its station; not pirate bases / nests / machine yard / finds) is a HAVEN (swoop range + 6 u; a world at WAR with you does not protect you). Pirates, the Machine Fleet + creatures never enter a haven (pushed out at its edge); while you are inside one they HOLD at the edge, can't charge / lunge, and their shots FIZZLE on it (cyan splash). space-fleets: every 0.4 s up to 2 free PATROL ships per held hostile INTERCEPT it ("<WORLD> PATROL ENGAGING. Friendly patrols are never foes (no lock-on, missiles, minimap red, fight camera). Camera: the swoop now ALWAYS happens near a model, fight or not. Belt serpents keep their own mine. space-combat ?v=s410b, space-creatures + space-fleets ?v=s410.

## s609 JOINTED FOX (elbows + knees on OUR player)
Backups: backup/joints/fox-kit.pre-joints.js, backup/joints/jointed-mirror.pre-joints.js.
- fox-kit.js jointLimbs(): the cast PLAYER (makeFox key 'player', or opts joints:true; joints:false turns it off) gets a FOREARM child at the elbow (P.fore) and a SHIN child at the knee (P.shin). Same split as Fox Fighters duel-foxes.js, but kept as CHILDREN of the arm / leg, so every existing pose, fighter-gear move, super, armour set and holster still works. Merge (phone) treats them as bones (+4 draws).
- animFox bendJoints(): soft elbows at rest, more on forward swings, knees lift on each forward step, tuck in the air; elbow straight while the laser / sword is out. Overrides: fox.userData.elbow = [e0, e1, z0, z1], fox.userData.knee = [k0, k1].
- rejoint(): armour / gear strapped on later below the joint moves into the forearm / shin (dressArmor still removes them fine).
- NEW engine/fox-poses.js applyPose(fox, name, t, k): cutscene / emote poses WAVE · POINT · HANDS ON HIPS · SHRUG · GUARD · JAB+CROSS · KNEEL · BOW · CHEER · THINK.
- Jointed Fox Mirror.dc.html (engine/jointed-mirror.js): OLD fox vs OUR FOX NOW, same input (move, 1 strike/draw, 2 laser, jump) + the pose buttons.
- NOT DONE: Hope (cane rig) + Noble (chair) keep the old arms; phone test 390x844 / 844x390; cutscene system calling applyPose.

Now: jointed arms are 30 % LONGER (fox-kit ARMK 1.3; tubes stretched, paws keep shape; armour strapped on later is stretched + re-parented the same way), and engine/fox-poses.js is TWO-BONE IK (paw / foot targets + elbow / knee pole), signature applyPose(THREE, fox, name, t, k). Mirror page: pose camera zooms in on the new fox, side view for KNEEL / BOW / POINT / PUNCH.

## s609c FOX ANIMATION LAB (Ben: "really polish a number of animations, with faces"; "hands / arms must never go inside the body or head")
- NEW Fox Animation Lab.dc.html (engine/fox-anim-lab.js): only our player, 18 animations in 3 groups, PAUSE / SLOW ¼ / AUTO CAM / FRONT / ¾ / SIDE, a live PAWS CLEAR check. Phone: stage top, buttons below; landscape: buttons on the right.
- engine/fox-poses.js rewritten as KEYFRAMES (anticipation, overshoot 'back' ease, holds) + fx layer (wave, shakes, taps, tremble, fist pumps) + idle breath. EMOTES: WAVE, YES (NOD), NO (ARMS FOLDED), SHRUG, LAUGH, CHEER, WINK · STORY: THINK, POINT, BOW, KNEEL, SALUTE, HANDS ON HIPS, FACEPALM, SCARED, YAWN + STRETCH · FIGHT: GUARD, JAB + CROSS.
- NO PAWS IN THE BODY: torso, hips, head + muzzle are ellipsoids; paw targets are pushed out + kept within reach, then the elbow swings out until elbow, forearm and paw are clear. Scan of all 18 (every 0.1 s): all clear. u.poseClear / u.poseDbg report it.
- FACES (fox-kit): new moods shock, sleepy, wink (right eye shut), squint; eyes can look up / down (lookY); u.faceHold { mouth, look, lookY, blink } lets a pose drive the jaw + eyes. Props: sweat drop on the head, "?" / "!" pop-up marks.
- Body lean / twist / roll now pivot at the HIPS; feet stay planted on the ground (hop lifts them). endPose(fox) clears everything.
- NEXT: Ben picks favourites / tweaks; call applyPose from cutscenes + dialogue (e.g. a line's emote); Hope + Noble joints.
- s609d HANDS (Ben: "fingers open and sometimes close into a fist"): fox-kit pawHand() for the jointed player: palm + pad, 4 fingers (2 bones; 1 on phones) + thumb on pivots (P.hands, P.handBones are merge bones). animFox handTick: u.grip [l, r] 0 open .. 1 fist, u.point [l, r] index out, u.spread; defaults relaxed half-curl, fist while the sword / laser is out. Every animation now sets its hands (open wave, fists in cheer / guard, finger guns in WINK, index out in POINT + THINK, flat salute, spread fingers in SCARED / SHRUG / YAWN). NEW HANDS group: OPEN + CLOSE, COUNT 1-2-3, GRAB; CLOSE-UP camera button. Backups: backup/joints/*.pre-hands.js. Phone cost: ≈ +20 draws on the player (2-bone fingers off on phones).
- s609e HAND ANATOMY (Ben's deep dive). fox-kit pawHand rebuilt: WRIST pivot g (Euler YXZ: y forearm twist, x flex, z side bend) at the top of the palm; index next to the thumb on BOTH hands (left hand was mirrored wrong); middle finger longest, pinky shortest, knuckles on an arc; 2-bone THUMB on the palm side (th, th2) + thumb-base pad. handTick: palm faces the thigh, thumb forward (twist s*1.37); finger CASCADE (index least curled, pinky most); curled fingers converge toward the thumb; open fingers fan; thumb blends REST (beside the index) → OPEN (≈50° L) → FIST (wraps OUTSIDE across index + middle) → OPPOSED (faces the fingers, grabbing) → UP. New u.thumbUp, u.oppose, u.fcurl/u.fcK (per finger), u.wrist.
  fox-poses: every animation sets palm direction (body space) + wrist; WAVE = palm to camera, paw lags the forearm (follow-through), fingers flick; SHRUG palms up; WINK finger guns with thumb hammer; GRAB = wrist cocks back, thumb opposes, close together; JAB corkscrews palm-down. NEW HAND STUDY group (paw camera orbit + anatomy notes): RELAXED, OPEN, FIST, THUMBS UP, FINGER WAVE. Backups backup/joints/*.pre-anatomy.js.
- s609f HAND FINAL POLISH + SOLID GAUNTLET (Ben: "the hand breaks through the gauntlet when waving"): fitCuff() measures the lowest cuff on each forearm (sleeve / plate / armour gauntlet / EVA glove, merged or not; re-measured when armour changes) and puts the WRIST pivot on its rim, so the palm always hangs below the gauntlet and only a slim fur wrist stub tucks inside. Wrist flex + side bend clamped to ±0.55 / ±0.5 and smoothed (fox-kit + fox-poses). Polish: little claws on each fingertip, a tiny living drift in relaxed fingers, softer wave follow-through. Backup backup/joints/fox-kit.pre-cuff.js.

SALUTE = clearly a BENT arm (≈60°), elbow out to the side at shoulder height, shoulder raised (new D.sh), flat paw with the fingertips at the brow ABOVE the eye (new per-arm head clearance D.hp so the paw can touch the brow); never a straight-arm salute. GUARD = fists apart beside the chin (face shows between), in front of the chest, elbows down + tucked, slow small breathing bob (was close together, jittering, behind the chest). JAB + CROSS land in front of the chin / chest line, clear of the muzzle. Collision shapes accept per-shape pad offsets; torso shape adjusts for taller legs.

Each ear = one cupped SHELL (earShell, cached per colours): convex back / hollow front, thick root → thin tip, tip bends back, root curves down onto the round skull and sinks into it; vertex colours: fur at the root fading into the dark back, dark rim round a pink bowl fading to cream at the base; a smooth inflated outline (inflate(), welded normals). 7 cream fluff tufts fan out of the bowl. The ROOT: a low fur mound on the skull as wide as the ear base and tilted with it + 4 fur tufts over the front seam (no bun, no gap when the ear moves). Fox Workshop ear sliders still apply. EAR LIFE in animFox: swivel toward where the eyes look, spring lag / flop when the head turns, random one-ear twitches, perk up + forward (surprised / excited / curious), airplane ears back + out (sad / shock / sleepy / squint). Old 3 dark cones replaced by: (1) CROWN SHADING cap (vertex colours, fur at the brow deepening to a darker crown + a darker stripe down the middle of the forehead); (2) a swept FORELOCK of 5 curved tapered locks (lockGeo: CatmullRom tube, tapered, flattened, root fur → furDark tip, inked) rooted on the front of the crown, rising then sweeping forward + to one side (away from a hair bow), tips curling; (3) 7 short CROWN FRINGE locks round the back between the ears + 5 NAPE locks down into the collar (no ink lines, just the furry silhouette). - s619b (Ben: "foot not actually on the ground when pushing"): skateD push stroke rebuilt: the back foot steps OFF the board onto the ground on the toe side (o.deckH = deck height, the park board passes its seat height), sweeps back along the board, lifts and returns to the deck; the front knee bends deep so it can reach (ankle ≈ ground level, checked in the lab).
- s619c PUSH STUDY (Ben: "face forward to push, then turn once going?"): skateD now does the real push: PREP (front foot pivots down the board, hips + shoulders turn to FACE the travel, weight on a bent front knee, eyes ahead) → PLANT (back foot steps down beside the board) → PUSH (sweeps back, leg straightening) with the opposite arm swinging → RECOVER (lift + swing forward, repeat) → SET (back foot on the tail, body turns sideways again, head keeps looking forward). o.pushK = how far turned (eased); the park board (vehicle-lab.js) eases pushK in when you push and out when you coast. Lab SKATE: PUSH + RIDE = turn, 3 pushes, set, carve (camera from the front of the board).
- s619d (Ben: "foot + leg going through the board"): push foot now plants OUTSIDE the board edge (o.boardHalfW, default 0.34 = the Meru board) the whole stroke, the knee points out, and stepping off / back on arcs UP over the edge instead of snapping through it. Checked every 0.1 s of PUSH + RIDE: thigh + shin never inside the deck.
- s619e (Ben: "stand in the middle on one leg"): while pushing, the standing foot sits in the MIDDLE of the board at the front bolts and the hips shift out over the push-side edge (D.bz 0.2), so the pushing leg drops nearly straight down beside the board. Checked every 0.1 s against the real deck (top 0.16, half width 0.34, leg radius 0.07-0.08): no overlap.
- s619f (Ben: "shoes cutting into the board when riding"): the Meru board's grip tape is at 0.31 (raycast), not 0.14: skateD default deckH 0.31 + lab fox stands at 0.31; every foot ON the deck is lifted by footUp 0.14 (the shoe sole sits below the IK foot point); the push foot's ankle rises as it sweeps back (the boot tips) so the sole stays ON the ground the whole stroke. Checked every 0.1 s: soles ≥ deck top when riding, 0.00-0.03 on the ground when pushing, no leg in the board.
- s619g (Ben: "floating way above the board"): footUp 0.14 was far too much at the new deck height; tuned to 0.058 by measuring the shoe soles: riding 0.30-0.32 against the deck top 0.313 (push / ride, kickflip), grind + ollie crouch 0.33-0.35.
- s619h (Ben: "go back to before the shoe fix, then just tilt the feet up"): reverted s619f/g (deckH default 0.14, lab fox at 0.14, push stroke as in s619e). New: D.ft [l, r] = toe-up tilt of the foot after the leg IK (applyD rotates the shin); skateD tilts every foot ON the deck 0.18 rad + lifts it 1.5 cm so the shoe edge no longer cuts the board.
